name: Customer_5939
comments:
Got to the restaurant and gave the name under our reservation. They don't take reservations and don't know why open table lists them but they get that a lot. Hmm ok. Can you try to do something for us since it isn't our fault you haven't contacted open table? No, 1 hr wait. No problem, we will go next door for drinks. Get text from restaurant that let's you check status through wait for out....opentable. Hmmmm.  Come back in an hr, get seated outside even though there are plenty of spaces inside. Fine. Drink wifey ordered was the best part of the experience.

Can we order the cauliflower - no, we are out of our most popular item. Ok.

Guac appetizer - made from half an avocado and a thousand chips. $12 

Salad with ahi - 1 dimensional salad with 3 pieces of ahi. Ahi was good wish there was more of it. Salad had no diversity anything interesting $23

Chicken kabobs - supposed to be with ginger terriyaki and sesame and garlic. Only thing I could taste
was terriyaki, very heavy handed.
 
Nothing we ordered was beyond marginal...

name: Customer_7468
comments: I don't get it. 4 and 5-start reviews abound, and the weekend brunch line is absurd, but I'd have to describe my experince at Tavern as "just okay." I went here on a Sunday morning ambigudate a month ago. We managed to get bar seating after waiting about 10 minutes, which seemed pretty good compared to the lengthy wait for a real table. The place was bustling, but we didn't have to wait too long to get in our drink orders. That said, while I love deals--and 2-for-1 mimosas and the like qualify--I wasn't bowled over. It tasted like a cheap cava and was heavy on the orange juice. I ordered a burger while my dining companion decided to go with the traditional brunch. My burger was decent but not mouthwateringly amazing, which makes it a far cry from many of the reviews claiming this to be the "best burger in Nashville." Similarly, despite the attempts to make the brunch fare a bit fancier, I wasn't bowled over by any of the flavors. While the prices aren't crazy expensive, they aren't cheap either. Overall I'd describe Tavern as "fine." I'd have no qualms about returning, but the foodie within me doesn't get the hype. Nashville, just because something is dressed up to look fancy and act fancy doesn't mean it's *actually* fancy.

name: Customer_3205
comments: Oh wow. Yummiest!  Sweet potato chips with warm blue cheese sauce. Awesome. Two for one drink special til 10 pm. Perfect. Philly cheese steak egg rolls that were to die for. Great night out. Probably too cool of a place for this old gal.  I wish I was hungrier.

name: Customer_4172
comments:
So... it took me a while to write this review but my visits have been so spread out in time. Bottom line is any way I love it!!!

My favorite server is Jaclyn and even though I got nothing but good service here I would say she's a superstar. So very helpful and friendly

Food wise I don't think you can go wrong. I have been all over the menu and had all good experience. Some of my favorites are the Parmesan fries, the buffalo cauliflower and the kale salad. The lettuce wraps are perfect if your not super hungry or just looking for something healthier, the black bean falafel is so yummy and their chimichanga is even better than Chuy's! 

The only bad thing is you can't book a table and it's usually a long wait in line, which I just hate.... bartenders are super hood working both the seated and people waiting behind so you can always get a drink at watch TV while waiting for your table. 
Watch out for the Saturday and Sunday brunches if you don't like a crowd, I love it though. The energy and the 2 for 1 mimosas, selected wines and spirits are a perfect start for your weekend morning. 

This is the perfect neighborhood restaurant that is neat, clean, romantic if you like or cool and full of sports if that

name: Customer_6882
comments:
Service was ok, but the food was excellent.  Nothing against our sweet server, but she was alone on a 20 person table - really? I completely blame that one on management! 

Buffalo cauliflower was awesome and the chicken skewers were so so good!  Everyone had a wonderful time! 

Ambiance was so fun!

name: Customer_4473
comments:
Food was average and did take a bit to come out Service was good.
Great local beer selection.  Had Chimichanga and burger and fries both were average but not outstanding. Great space/ bar.

name: Customer_1881
comments: From service to taste this restaurant had it all. Their mahi sandwich was cooked and seasoned perfectly. Their drink selection was vast and test

name: Customer_5553
comments: Meet by a great hostess at the door, Jenna. Her smile was amazing! Drinks at the bar were rather good.  They actually have a loco moco! BOOM!

name: Customer_2398
comments: I came here for my birthday brunch and was pleasantly surprised! Our server was wonderful and she talked a lot with us and made the experience even better! Every single dish ordered from our table was delicious! Definitely one of he best brunch places in Nashville!

name: Customer_9700
comments: We came here because of all the great yelp reviews, I can't believe this is 4-stars.. Good beer selection, good atmosphere, and decent service. The food, however, was bla.. We really wanted to try the fried chicken skins, they came out very hard and very stuck together. The sauce had good flavor but the skins came in a clump that we could hardly break apart. Our food came out about 4 minutes into our attempt to chisel the skins apart. Kaya toast was weird and really lacked anything to bring the dish together. After scraping off the sauce it was basically Texas toast and an egg. The 2 sets of tacos we ordered were both overcooked and VERY dry. Come here for drinks, skip the food!

name: Customer_1124
comments:
Went here for a Saturday morning brunch and it wasn't that bad! 

Cons: the wait is crazy long (over an hour), the lighting is a bit dark, the music and atmosphere is crazy loud so prepare to scream your conversations, the drinks (specifically the mimosa) wasn't that strong and the food was good but average.

Pros: It's a nice trendy spot with fun music that you'll want to sing along to (especially after drinks). The staff was very attentive and friendly! And the prices aren't that bad (for downtown).

All in all it was a nice experience, but don't think I'll be in a hurry to go back.

name: Customer_7644
comments: I finally got to come and experience brunch here! Which is easier said than done. I've attempted to come before and the wait was around 1.5-2 hours. On Sunday we came around 1115 for a 45 minute wait which wasn't bad for a group of 5. It's two for ones for Sunday brunch and I tried the sangria and the blood orange mimosa. I preferred the sangria hands down! For food I ordered the huevos rancheros which was pretty good. My gf ordered the Singapore stiryfry and the white trash hash and I liked her stir fry a lot! I will be back for sure because I keep hearing how good the tavern burger is and I won't make the mistake of not ordering it next time! Awesome atmosphere with a brunch of tvs. Can be a little loud though.

name: Customer_2063
comments: Good drinks, good food and a great atmosphere! What more could you want? The drink menu is very extensive, good selection of scotch and cocktails. The food was very impressive as well. I tried the sweet potato fries with jalapeno mayo after seeing it suggested so much and I must say they delivered! This is a great place to hang out with friends and pass some time. Give it a try!

name: Customer_5032
comments:
The simply-named Tavern offers up some mighty simple comfort food pleasures (White Trash hash, anyone?) and elevated junk food game bites. 

That said, I'm not sure this is quite the weekend brunch place for me, due to the TVs providing all of the background noise. I'm not a fan of big TVs blaring games -- to me, this is the worst kind of ambiance. BUT... for those of you seeking a place to watch local sports and cheer on with a crowd, Tavern is the spot for you, especially if your tastes are a bit more high brow than your typical nachos. I mean, they have nachos, but Tavern's come with pistachio and goat cheese. Nice! 

I'd easily return on a non game day (or even to sit on the shaded side patio) for more of that White Trash Hash. Think tater tot casserole. I mean, really. Goodbye hangover. The egg white omelet I had was kinda blah, as the tomatoes made it seem extra watery.The "Wicked" Bloody Mary was hardly wicked, more like gentle, despite the vodka being infused with pickled things that you'd hope for on your glass. They don't automatically garnish the way you'd think. Or at least the way a New Orleanian would think. I mean... just a lime? Nu uh. Our very lovely server came out with some olives for us, which was nice. But a Bloody without beaucoup d' garnish is a naked Mary, indeed.

Extra props for three bottles of hot sauces on the table, marked X, XX and XXX. Go for the orangey habanero, as it's the tastiest of the bunch (it might be the XX). Don't be fooled by the warnings. They are there for the bland American palate.

name: Customer_9424
comments: PSA: Just go for the 2 for 1 drink special at brunch and white trash hash.  The atmosphere is trendy. Everything else is not worth the wait! We arrived at 11am on a Friday for brunch, was told the wait was 20 mins. We did not get seated until 11:50a. Food is average. I will say the nachos were good but nothing outstanding. The biscuits came out cold. A "side" of bacon is $5 dollars and you get seriously 2 slices. Service was very very slow. Wouldn't recommend unless you have 3.5 hours or more  to kill for brunch.

name: Customer_9011
comments: Tavern is THE Nashville brunch spot. {starters} I have tried a good portion of the starter selections - but the buffalo cauliflower, brussels and tavern fries stand out above the rest. The mussels are also a great option for dinner or happy hour. {entrees} I'm a huge fan of benedicts, and Tavern kills it with each of their 3 options - aptly named uno, dos, and (for some reason) three. Uno is my favorite, with braised short rib and Tobasco hollandaise. It is absolutely delicous. Other great options are the Nooner - which is a bacon scramble with fried oysters and spicy sour cream - and the Singapore Stir-fry, with wok-style rice, a sunny-side-up egg, and bacon. You really can't go wrong with any of the Tavern's fantastic brunch selections, but these stand out for sure. {libations} Possibly the reason that Tavern is so popular among Nashville brunch-goers, is the 2-for-1 deal they offer during brunch all weekend. The selection is fairly standard, with mimosas, a bellini, two bloody mary renditions, and a very sweet sangria. My favorite is the blood orange mimosa, but each drink has its merits. Overall, Tavern is a wonderful place for any brunch occasion and I will continue to dine here often as long as I am in Nashville. The wait is brutal so make sure you arrive early to start off with a beverage in the sun on their outdoor waiting area. Enjoy!

name: Customer_7000
comments:
Tavern is great for brunch, lunch or dinner. The atmosphere is casual, yet classy, with dim lighting as well as some natural light above the bar and in the front room of the restaurant. There are TVs for watching sports as well. In the Midtown area of downtown, this M Street restaurant has a nice bar and cozy half-moon booths. There is also a street-side patio (with very uncomfortable, wrought iron circle tables that do not fit well with the permanent wood bench) and valet parking.

For brunch, the white trash hash is a must with any dish. The cheddar cheese biscuits with chorizo gravy and turkey BLT were great savory dishes, but I have heard amazing things about the red velvet waffles.

For lunch and dinner, don't go with the grilled cheese. The menu has so much more to offer, and it's not the greatest grilled cheese I've ever had. The guacamole was a small serving, but fresh and with great flavor. The sweet potato chips with blue cheese fondue is to die for! I'm not a huge blue cheese fan, but this is the best cheese dip/fondue I've ever had! The chips are served fresh and warm. The mussels are also amazing, with bacon adding a unique taste. 

As for drinks, the strawberry balsamic martini is my favorite drink (on their menu and in the world).  Its sweet, with a small kick from the balsamic. Their whiskey drinks are strong and the berry julep is a good choice.

Overall, this is a great restaurant for any occasion from a business lunch to a hungover Sunday brunch. Be aware, they do NOT take reservations, which can be very frustrating, but the wait is worth it.

name: Customer_8421
comments: Hmmmmm it's decent. Not sure about the 'rave' reviews to be honest. The prices kind of turned me off. They have a brunch item of Kaya Toast which is to out it bluntly ridiculously overpriced. I can get a jar of Kaya from the Asian market for 1/10the price of the dish. Not impressed.

name: Customer_5714
comments: Dark wood, open warm space and welcoming service.  It seems the owners of Tavern have their hand on the pulse of the Vandy area.  The patio cushioned banquet seating perfect for people watching.  The patio is open and inviting, the interior is spacious and bustling.  I had wine, chicken tacos and Yukon truffle chips.  I must say the chips were my favorite, perfect for trying all the sauces on the table.  They were warm and crispy.  The tacos were a bit tough and chewy.  I will defiantly be back to conquer that burger!  Chow!

name: Customer_3866
comments: Y'all gave my Asian friend and my white friend some food poisoning from the Caesar salad. Thanks Obama.

name: Customer_9652
comments: I've been to Tavern three times, and each time this "happy hour" (quotes due to the fact that actual happy hour is only on Wednesdays) location was chosen by or because of guy friends. Why do men love this place?? Maybe it's the industrial concrete or the weird chains on the wall? Anyway, the food really is good - I recommend the nachos, guac or lobster hushpuppies, just don't be shocked when you get your pricey check at the end of the night. The drinks are only reasonably priced if you go on 2-4-1 Wednesday - unless you follow the lead of the d-bag at our table last night and walk out on your check. If you're going with a large group make sure you get there early since they don't take reservations or let you call ahead. They also charge a $15 cake fee if you bring a dessert on a special occasion, even though they have no desserts on the menu. It's not a bad place - it's in a good location, has good food and a cool vibe, I just prefer something a little cheaper and more low key. If you share my preference for a midtown happy hour, allow me to suggest Brewhouse or Corner Pub instead.

name: Customer_4351
comments:
The simply-named Tavern offers up some mighty simple comfort food pleasures (White Trash hash, anyone?) and elevated junk food game bites. 

That said, I'm not sure this is quite the weekend brunch place for me, due to the TVs providing all of the background noise. I'm not a fan of big TVs blaring games -- to me, this is the worst kind of ambiance. BUT... for those of you seeking a place to watch local sports and cheer on with a crowd, Tavern is the spot for you, especially if your tastes are a bit more high brow than your typical nachos. I mean, they have nachos, but Tavern's come with pistachio and goat cheese. Nice! 

I'd easily return on a non game day (or even to sit on the shaded side patio) for more of that White Trash Hash. Think tater tot casserole. I mean, really. Goodbye hangover. The egg white omelet I had was kinda blah, as the tomatoes made it seem extra watery.The "Wicked" Bloody Mary was hardly wicked, more like gentle, despite the vodka being infused with pickled things that you'd hope for on your glass. They don't automatically garnish the way you'd think. Or at least the way a New Orleanian would think. I mean... just a lime? Nu uh. Our very lovely server came out with some olives for us, which was nice. But a Bloody without beaucoup d' garnish is a naked Mary, indeed.

Extra props for three bottles of hot sauces on the table, marked X, XX and XXX. Go for the orangey habanero, as it's the tastiest of the bunch (it might be the XX). Don't be fooled by the warnings. They are there for the bland American palate.

name: Customer_3264
comments:
One of the best brunch spots in town.  Get there early though because the secret was out long ago. Trying to get in on a sat/sun around 11-1 and you are probably looking at an hour plus wait. Why is it so popular? It probably has to do with the 2-4-1 cocktails, or maybe the red velvet waffles with cream cheese drizzle, or perhaps it's the signature "white trash hash"... a delicious concoction of cheese, hash browns, and scallions rolled into an almost crispy-shelled ball of tasty delight.  They have takes on all the traditional brunch classics as well... a variety of egg/benedict themed plates, waffles, and of course biscuits.  

What I really like is that for all the heavy brunch menu items they have there is also a whole "skinny" section devoted entirely to those who are taking it light and counting calories. An egg white scramble, yogurt, and salads are among some of the things you will find on that menu. The brunch libations don't really pull any punches even though drinks are buy one get one free. Bloody Marys, trumped up Mimosas, and my favorite, the red berry sangria. 

My advice is to get there right when they open at 10am. There will be a few people already lined up but you won't wait.  You'll be glad you did because by the time you leave the waiting area will be packed and you'll be able to walk out happy knowing you didn't have to sit through all that mess.

name: Customer_7796
comments: Meh. I don't see how this place got such high marks. We started off with the cauliflower buffalo bites and steak and cheese egg rolls. The cauliflower bites were kind of soggy/a little overdone. The cheese steak egg rolls were nothing to write home about either. They were served up with what tasted like a hunts ketchup dip and a cheese dip straight out of a jar. I ordered the turkey BLT and asked for an extra side of the avocado aioli. The aioli did not taste like avocado. The turkey BLT should just be called a turkey sandwich because BLTs should contain a decent amount of bacon and lettuce. My sandwich came with a sliver of bacon and even less lettuce. It was stacked with turkey but it needed way more lettuce to help freshen it up. It was served with sweet potato chips that were soaked in oil. 1/4 were edible and the rest were to drenched in oil to even think about eating. I don't know why our food took so long. For sure they weren't back there frying up fresh chips for me.

name: Customer_1321
comments: Y'all gave my Asian friend and my white friend some food poisoning from the Caesar salad. Thanks Obama.

name: Customer_2113
comments: I'm usually a chilaquiles girl, so the Huevos Rancheros sounded sort of tempting with its eggs, tortillas and salsa combination. Now, huevos rancheros in general has never really appealed to me, but Tavern had me changing my tune. I have a feeling that no other restaurant's version of this dish will impress me as much as this one, but if you are in Nashville and you are at Tavern for brunch and you don't get the Huevos Rancheros.... you're making a HUGE mistake. One of the best brunch meals of my life y'all...

name: Customer_2077
comments: From service to taste this restaurant had it all. Their mahi sandwich was cooked and seasoned perfectly. Their drink selection was vast and test

name: Customer_5876
comments: After drinking a few glasses of 1920 (the best cocktail in Nashville if you ask me), I am the happiest girl around! I also love the menu, it's fun without being weird. I can't stop eating the Philly cheesesteak eggrolls, brown bag special, all the different fries, and the kale salad.

name: Customer_2970
comments:
Tavern is probably one of the better brunch places in Nashville IF (and only if) you go with friends. This is not the place to go for a brunch date or to go with any person that you actually want to have a conversation with.

Both times that my wife and I have gone (once by ourselves, and the other time with some friends) the music has been extremely loud - like to the point where we have been yelling just to hear each other. Not kidding. Look, I like my music loud... and their playlist was actually on point (late 90's/early 2000's hits)... but going out to eat is a social experience. Part of sharing a meal is enjoying the company of the people you're with. Don't blast music in my face and force me to lean in just to hear what the person next to me is saying. C'mon. 

On to the food! It's GREAT. I highly recommend the Benedict Uno - a short rib benedict topped with tabasco-infused hollandaise. Wow. So much amazing flavor in every bite. I savored it right down to the end. I also recommend the maple fondue if you're with a group. It's a fun dish to share and has assorted fruits and some french toast and sausage... all to be dipped in a delicious warm maple syrup mixture. Can't go wrong. Also, don't sleep on the 2-for-1 libations. The blood orange mimosa and the red sangria are my favorites (although the last time I went, I just doubled up on the sangria... easily my favorite).

This place deserves respect for the quality of food they put out and their decent pricing (average about $12-$15 per entree). The only things that keep this from being a 4-star review are the noise level, the lack of parking (bring cash because you will need to use the valet), and the fact that you will undoubtedly have a wait. When we went with our friends, we got their 10 minutes after they opened and were told there was a 20-30 minute wait. We ended up actually waiting almost an hour. Not really a complaint, since you have to factor in a wait at popular places... but still. Just a warning - you will have a wait.

Give this place a shot if you like good food for brunch, just go in knowing that there are some pitfalls with this place.

name: Customer_2631
comments:
Tavern has Nashville's best burger. I was sad when it was gone. Fantastic.

The staff is friendly, and the service is great. They even brought our group free s'mores. (That's right: They have s'mores.)

I have a new favorite Nashville restaurant.

name: Customer_5067
comments: Amazing bloody Mary's! We went there yesterday and their "brunch" was between 10-3 and consisted of 2 for 1 bloody Mary's. The place was packed and had to sit outside. Would recommend they actually turn the heat lamps on when it's 35 degrees out! Get here early to get a seat! We didn't try the food but the menu looked great.

name: Customer_9444
comments: Our food was pretty. The restaurant is decorated really nice and lots of seating. We got the mussels appetizer which was amazing! I got a wedge salad and my husband got the bbq ribs tacos. I liked talking to the server Zack, he was really nice and a good server. I would go back there just for the mussels!!

name: Customer_2557
comments: Excellent food and srvice!!! They even put my Mets game on the big screen. Order the chicken skins for an appetizer - freaking yummy!!! Burgers were great - Service is 5 star!!! Friend had the Lobster sliders - very good!!!

name: Customer_9404
comments:
Food tastes good but not worth the price. Drinks are overpriced as well. $11.50 for a small Moscow mule with stolii vodka. 

I got the grilled cheese and the grilled chicken skewers. Both tasted fine but nothing to write home about. The chicken came with rice but everything was very plain, nothing that would warrant the price I paid. My tab totaled $61 after tip for grilled cheese, chicken skewers, a beer, and a Moscow mule. 

For this reason I would not go back.

name: Customer_7861
comments: Oh, Brunch at Tavern. I'm so sad that it took me so long to visit you. I'll keep this brief: The dishes here are superbly crafted. Flavors are lovely and multifaceted, and the plating is gorgeous. My favorite dishes, though, are easy to pinpoint. First up is the Sweet Potato Chips, which arrive at your table with a curry salt and blue cheese fondue. This is a perfect start to any meal, and honestly, I could probably be happy just munching on these while sipping a few cocktails (which I'll get to in a moment). As for a main course, though: The Benedict Dos. Poached eggs, smoked salmon, and a creamy hollandaise? Delicious doesn't even begin to cover it. I will admit that I find myself rather addicted to their Blood Orange Mimosa, so I haven't actually tried anything else on the menu. However, one of my closest friends loved the Bloody Mary, and their beer selection is impressive and was mat with easy approval from our group a few weeks ago. Is it loud? Yes. Is it expensive? Sure, although most of the cocktails are two for one. But is it worth the insanely long wait? Absolutely.

name: Customer_2376
comments: Sunday Funday !!!! Best place to go on Sunday!!!! Excellent breakfast/brunch! If you got to watch your football/ ice hockey playoffs- any sports! This is the place!

name: Customer_4757
comments: Go for the buffalo cauliflower! What better combination could you ask for?! The drinks also are delicious. The space is large and draws a mix after work - a great place for happy hour.

name: Customer_9099
comments: Delicious food in a fun setting.  Great helpful and friendly service.  Two levels of seating near the bar.  We had awesome buffalo cauliflower, egg rolls with philly cheese steak and amazing kale salad.  highly recommend the Tavern.

name: Customer_4672
comments:
The food here is outstanding. I generally get the Tavern Burger, which is legitimately one of the best in town. The desserts are great as well; for instance, they let you make s'mores at your table. Furthermore, the beer selection is fairly robust, usually with several local breweries on tap. 

The downside here is the service. First, it's usually quite slow, even when the dining room is not too busy. It's taken over an hour to get my lunch before, and not during peak hours. However, the pace does not bother me as much as some of the staff's snooty demeanor. The hostesses in particular are generally a bit condescending, which is off-putting. The wait staff themselves are usually a bit better; you can tell they work for tips, whereas the hostesses quite clearly do not. All in all a good spot for lunch or supper, though.

name: Customer_5637
comments: Stopped by while on a business trip after reading other reviews. I had the salmon and it was really good. Only knock I have is that the portion size was really small (I thought, anyway). Also had the kale salad which was really good. I was trying to be good, but definitely had order envy when I saw the burger and fries. Give it a try! I would defintely go back!

name: Customer_3505
comments: So cute! A must stop on your Nashville adventure!!! Cutest drinks and brunch spot. I got the red sangria and an egg white and fruit brunch. My friends for mimosas. We are all so happy!

name: Customer_4983
comments: Chose Tavern because I wanted to catch a baseball game on their TVs while eating.  The wait for a table of four was an hour on a Saturday night.  Food was fine but nothing to jump up and down about.  Waitress recommended the Tavern burger...it was ok.

name: Customer_4637
comments: Tavern has a great brunch situation if you are looking to have drinks. 2 for 1 mimosas, bellinis, bloody Mary's and sangria make for a great start to the day. Brunch can get very packed during peak hours so you want to get there early on Saturdays and Sundays.

name: Customer_3252
comments: I got the bazooka toast, it was amazing! A little bit pricey but totally worth it. So good it inspired me to give my first yelp review :)

name: Customer_2461
comments: We stopped here for lunch/dinner and wasn't disappointed. We was seated and served drinks promptly. Had a difficult time deciding what to order cause everything looked delicous. I ordered the brown bag meal. Which is a thick cut grilled bologna and over-easy egg sandwich with homemade potato hips, with truffle oil.

name: Customer_3674
comments:
I really must admit, I am a fan of some tavern CUISINE.

Lets start with the guacamole.... 
(which is laced with pistachios and goat cheese mind you)
i would say...TO DIE FOR.

The fish taco's are SIMPLY divine, and could quite possibly be my very favorite in all of Nashville.

the Perogies are delish and add a nice touch to the menu... ( i hale from North Eastern Pennsylvania where this particular dish is a standard and i was not disappointed) 

The Shishito Peppers are perfect....
The Salads are fresh and refreshing...

I can not wait to return and sample some more tasty delights.

name: Customer_7678
comments: We waited an hour and a half to eat at this restaurant for a party of 3. We sat at the bar where they offered 2 for 1 drinks. 2 drinks for the price of 1!! What could be better? Towards the end of our hour and a half wait we began to get to hungry so we ordered some fries. They were very yummy!! Since eating the fries, by the time we got our table and ordered a meal, I wasn't very hungry. So I didn't  eat much of the omelette I ordered. So I don't have much feedback for that.

name: Customer_1359
comments: We stumbled onto this restaurant after seeing the very long line at Hattie B's. The atmosphere seemed really nice and the wait for a table much more manageable-only 10 minutes. The menu choices were appealing and we put in an order for two burgers, fries, a fish sandwich and trail salad. Then we waited, and waited and waited some more. Fifty minutes later our food still did not arrive with no real explanation (or apology) from our server. The manager was pleasant and after she was alerted our food did arrive. The burgers were tasty as were the Belgian fries. The trail mix salad had too many dried cranberries for my liking making it much too sweet. I think with a different server the expereince may have been more positive, but with so many great restaurants in Nashville I won't be going back to find out.

name: Customer_1517
comments: I've been here twice now, and the food is always great and the servic is decent. The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because the food takes a while to come out, even when it's not super busy. I've gotten the fish tacos (they are HUGE), burgers, fries (also huge portions), and goat cheese and pistachio guacamole. Like I said, the food is always very good, but if you're coming on a weekend, be prepared for a very long wait. It has a super hip atmosphere and you'll find a lot of twenty-somethings there.

name: Customer_7587
comments:
First time back to Nashville since I was in high school, and can't believe I haven't been back sooner! Here at Vanderbilt for a class, and kept passing by the Tavern on my way to campus each morning... Had an inticing, rustic, downtown Manhattan look to it. So I put it on my list of places to check out. I looked here in Yelp, and saw it had great reviews. 

I came in for dinner tonight, and immediately noticed the reclaimed wood door, wrought iron, and alternative rock playing. I knew it would be a great place. I sat at the bar, as I was here by myself, and immediately got a menu and was offered a drink. I had the 1920, which was a little stout, but better than weak, am I right? I ordered the lamb tacos, Tennessee tavern fries, and cinnamon roll bread pudding. Tacos were small, but honestly a decent portion considering how much meat was on them. They were hot out of the kitchen, and the roasted peanuts gave it great crunch. Now, the Tennessee tavern fries ... Sweet potato fries with a touch of cinnamon and sugar, with jalapeño ketchup. Shut the front door, these were to die for. Light and airy, arrived in a mini frying basket with abundant portions. The ketchup was amazing, and I definitely asked for more. The cinnamon roll bread  pudding was a muffin size portion, with vanilla ice cream, homemade whip, and caramel sauce. Great flavor, not overwhelming. 

Service was fantastic, and even met some fun people! Highly recommend this place. I'll be coming back for sure.

name: Customer_1046
comments: Terrible wait (unnecessary), average service, above average prices, and excruciating wait for food. Find someplace else. There's lots to choose from.

name: Customer_5437
comments: Honesty hour, we went out in Nashville after 10pm. Apparently, there are limited options at that time, when it isn't the weekend. We decided to try out this place after walking to a couple of other places that were not like their descriptions. This place has a nice ambience, nice staff, and a ton of beers and ciders on tap. The prices weren't bad for the drinks or beer. Between 5-8 for the beer/cider. Around 10-12 for cocktails. Oh, and the kitchen closes at 11. Now on to the food, we got the burger and the chimichanga. We were splitting them so we went for something a little different with the chimichanga. We also got the cheesesteak egg rolls. Sounds fantastic, right? Unfortunately, the burger was the only highlight. Everything else got a HUGE FAIL! The chimichanga was super soggy. The rice and beans were ok. The cheesesteak egg rolls were just BAD! No taste at all. Now on to our drinks. We first ordered their take on a margarita. They used silver Tequila so it had a very heavy tequila taste. It was ok. He wound up with the punch. It was ok. Mind you, we were traveling all day and ate everything. So, it was edible. All and all, if you need somewhere to go late, then try it. Just stick to very regular things. The staff is nice ,so, that is worth a visit based on that alone.

name: Customer_5079
comments:
Best place within walking distance from my hotel.  It's a pretty modern and happening place, with a cool feel to it.

I really was looking for a good salad, and was pleasantly surprised with my Junk Salad (romaine, salami, shrimp, olives, pepperoncini, hearts of palm, grape tomato, cucumber, blue cheese, champagne dijon vinaigrette).  This was a super tasty salad.

I came back 4 days later and had the burger and sweet potato ships.  Burger was pretty good, and my only complaint was that the chips were a little on the salty side.  Brush some of the salt off and it was good.

comments:
