name: Customer_1807
comments: I used to go to tavern pretty frequently over the past few years and was SHOCKED at the experince last night. A friend and I ordered the bazooka toast - described as "bazooka guacamole/bread/smoked salmon/fried egg/arugula" for a hefty $16! When we got our food we were floored... one piece of bread covered in a sort of smoked salmon spread... a far cry from the fresh slices of smoked salmon that one would expect from that description. Really disappointing, it looked and smelled like canned salmon or cat food? Really weird ...it should be described differently on the menu!

name: Customer_8827
comments: One of my favorite spots in town. Burger is amazing, good vibe, nice staff. Go-to gastro pub for sure.

name: Customer_2287
comments: Just stopped in for drinks. Staff was great, never felt rushed. Food passing by smelt and looked awesome. May be coming back tomorrow.

name: Customer_3060
comments: Well, the concept seems cool....but, not great service. The waitress forgot our drinks - we has finished our appetizer and they had not arrived, so we cancelled them. We tried to order 1 of the 3 late night dinner entrees they offered, but they were all out. Umm, bummer. We left and I don't think we will be back.

name: Customer_8954
comments: A good place. Kind of on the loud side, but a nice place. Fried chicken skins were superior. Rest of food was good and waitress was fairly attentive and kind of tuned in. Not a place to go if you're in a hurry.

name: Customer_7144
comments: Tavern is a great place to grab a late night bite. The menu has a lot of variety. I really enjoy the kale salad and all their fries. The s'mores dessert is also really fun and unique! Definitely worth checking out if you're in midtown Nashville.

name: Customer_6355
comments: Excellent service, has air conditioning which is great in the south, my favorite was the chicken chicharrón "chicharrón" good location in the block is the best one!

name: Customer_5228
comments: One of the best burgers in Nashville, definitely the best 'upscale' burger I've found, and some really nice well-mixed drinks to go with them. The crowd gets a bit overrun with frat-types on Friday and Saturday nights, but it's a great place for a lunch or weeknight drink/dinner.

name: Customer_6685
comments: Great burgers!  Still full in the morning with a meat hangover.  Fries were excellent too.  Service was good.  Busy night but felt taken care of.  Highly recommend.

name: Customer_3966
comments: My husband and I are visiting Nashville from Chicago (go cubs). We have been to tavern once before last year and my husband fell in love with the chickenooga drink. So in love that tavern was our first stop back in town. Well, one chickenooga into the night and there was an issue with the keg equipment making this drink unavailable. The manager soon came over with a substitute option replacing the beer. They very well could have just said "too bad" but went way above and beyond and made my husband content. Great food too but the servic is well above the rest!

name: Customer_6177
comments: Was not too much a fan of some of the food. The Lamb was not lamb have no clue why it was. However the staff is very nice and the drinks were great.

name: Customer_5115
comments: We totally blew off all Nashville brunch recommendations just because the menu at Tavern looked so good. Risky move, bucking the suggestions of former residents and frequent visitors, but I'm happy to report it paid off handsomely. I looove the set-up of the restaurant. There's a covered/open air area, a bar area with some booths and high-top tables, then a cozy area "upstairs" overlooking the action so to speak. It basically has a seating location for whatever your mood. Very cool. The brunch menu was almost impossible to choose from. Our eyes went directly to the red velvet waffle with cream cheese drizzle. We're not big sweets for breakfast folks but we do love our desserts. But the inevitable was sure to occur, eat brunch and be too full - rule of thumb - order your sweets at the same time as your meal if you're determined to try something. So we did.... I opted for the benedict uno which was fantastic. Tender braised short ribs on an english muffin with perfectly cooked poached eggs and a Tabasco hollandaise. Soooo incredibly good and the hollandaise was the perfect combination of buttery and spicy. Excellent. I will say, if you don't love hollandaise you would be put off - my plate was literally swimming in sauce (arm floaties and all...) I gobbled it up but it turned my wife off from trying it (note to self, don't bath in hollandaise.) My wife opted for the The Nooner which is an omelet with bacon, fried oysters and a spicy sour cream, served with "white trash hash" (basically a heavily hashbrown casserole.) So back to the red velvet wafftle....we didn't finish it....I know...I know....we tried and we did a pretty good job, but we just couldn't. It was super good although almost not quite done in the middle, but tasty nonetheless. Good service, good food, great atmosphere (would love to watch a game here and snack my way through the day.) Can't wait to return!

name: Customer_9795
comments: Went on a friend's birthday for a birthday dinner and had a very bad experience. A very long wait despite having reservations, and then it took forever just to get a drink from the bar. The food was very, very disappointing--I ordered the lettuce wraps and left hungry. We split a few appetizers, including the crudite/hummus plate--I was just shocked at how overpriced it all was. This is definitely for the yuppie set that doesn't mind spending $ on mediocre food.

name: Customer_3094
comments:
I've only been to Tavern once and it was for Sunday brunch. 
My friend and I wanted somewhere close to our church (Midtown 12South) and she suggested Tavern because she said the brunch food was good. I wasn't too sure about the meal I ended up ordering...you know how you have those days where you teeter back and forth between what to order and then end up just blurting out a choice and don't really know if you're ok with what you said? Well...this one of those times, so it might have skewed my verdict. The food was good, but it wasn't my favorite. The 2for1 brunch drinks helped a bit. 

I might would go back and try some lunch food and see how that is. But for now, it's just A-ok in my book.

name: Customer_1223
comments: Everything is wonderful at The Tavern!!!!. The service is outstanding. The seafood choices are plentiful. The skillet bread is  so so good! I love the portion size..just right. The Chocolate chip cookie skillet dessert is super super delicious! We have gone on a Sunday night a few times a it's semi- quiet and it's a delightful Sunday meal.

name: Customer_4810
comments: Tavern has a nice variety of healthy options. They have a large section titled "yolks" which consists of the many different and funky ways you can serve an egg (we had one with salmon in an omelette and it was delicious). We also had the "trail mix" which consisted of bulgur, quinoa, and other healthy perks... a great way to start the morning. 2/1 brunch libations - I would recomend the Cucumber Mary.

name: Customer_8032
comments: So cute! A must stop on your Nashville adventure!!! Cutest drinks and brunch spot. I got the red sangria and an egg white and fruit brunch. My friends for mimosas. We are all so happy!

name: Customer_3386
comments: I used to go to tavern pretty frequently over the past few years and was SHOCKED at the experience last night. A friend and I ordered the bazooka toast - described as "bazooka guacamole/bread/smoked salmon/fried egg/arugula" for a hefty $16! When we got our food we were floored... one piece of bread covered in a sort of smoked salmon spread... a far cry from the fresh slices of smoked salmon that one would expect from that description. Really disappointing, it looked and smelled like canned salmon or cat food? Really weird ...it should be described differently on the menu!

name: Customer_9048
comments: My 8 friends and I came here during our visit to Nashville because of good reviews we heard from friends who visited - they did not disappoint. Tavern was a great brunch spot and they were able to accommodate our large group fairly easily. The service was awesome, relaxed and friendly staff all around. The food was phenomenal - We split almost every app on the menu, all very good. I had the special taco scramble and it was one of the best egg dishes I've had in a while. The "white trash hash" that came with it was delicious and a twist on the classic hashbrowns. All in all I would come back here and would recomand to anyone visiting.

name: Customer_4379
comments: Came for brunch on Fathers Day, packed!  We were able to get a spot at the bar right away and ate there. Food was above average and the bartenders were quick and attentive.

name: Customer_3780
comments: PSA: Just go for the 2 for 1 drink special at brunch and white trash hash. The atmosphere is trendy. Everything else is not worth the wait! We arrived at 11am on a Friday for brunch, was told the wait was 20 mins. We did not get seated until 11:50a. Food is average. I will say the nachos were good but nothing outstanding. The biscuits came out cold. A "side" of bacon is $5 dollars and you get seriously 2 slices. Service was very very slow. Wouldn't recommend unless you have 3.5 hours or more to kill for brunch.

name: Customer_2102
comments: Food was so good! Great music, good casual or event atmosphere. Came here for a group birthday dinner. Their white sangria was amazing

name: Customer_4184
comments: Place was awesome! Went here for my birthday & I had a large party of 12, they included gratuity with the bill. But the waitress was very nice! Good music & environment. I will definitely be coming to this place again!!!

name: Customer_2701
comments: First time back to Nashville since I was in high school, and can't believe I haven't been back sooner! Here at Vanderbilt for a class, and kept passing by the Tavern on my way to campus each morning... Had an inticing, rustic, downtown Manhattan look to it. So I put it on my list of places to check out. I looked here in Yelp, and saw it had great reviews. I came in for dinner tonight, and immediately noticed the reclaimed wood door, wrought iron, and alternative rock playing. I knew it would be a great place. I sat at the bar, as I was here by myself, and immediately got a menu and was offered a drink. I had the 1920, which was a little stout, but better than weak, am I right? I ordered the lamb tacos, Tennessee tavern fries, and cinnamon roll bread pudding. Tacos were small, but honestly a decent portion considering how much meat was on them. They were hot out of the kitchen, and the roasted peanuts gave it great crunch. Now, the Tennessee tavern fries ... Sweet potato fries with a touch of cinnamon and sugar, with jalapeño ketchup. Shut the front door, these were to die for. Light and airy, arrived in a mini frying basket with abundant portions. The ketchup was amazing, and I definately asked for more. The cinnamon roll bread pudding was a muffin size portion, with vanilla ice cream, homemade whip, and caramel sauce. Great flavor, not overwhelming. Service was fantastic, and even met some fun people! Highly recommend this place. I'll be coming back for sure.

name: Customer_6658
comments: Service was ok, but the food was excellent. Nothing against our sweet server, but she was alone on a 20 person table - really? I completely blame that one on management! Buffalo cauliflower was awesome and the chicken skewers were so so good! Everyone had a wonderful time! Ambiance was so fun!

name: Customer_9711
comments: Drinks were strong! Guacamole and fries were excellent. Beef short rib tacos were like chewing on a tire. Mahi sandwich was overcooked and super fishy. Tried this place a few years ago, never came back but thought we would give it another shot. Probably won't be back, maybe for guacamole and fries. Our server was awesome though.

name: Customer_8378
comments: Terrible wait (unnecessary), average service, above average prices, and excruciating wait for food. Find someplace else. There's lots to choose from.

name: Customer_6251
comments:
my favorite brunch spot on nashville! 

the drinks are amazing and they have a wide range of items on the menu. my favorite brunch items are probably the benedicts and white trash hash.

my favorite items served all day are the sweet potato fries and tuscan kale salad!

the only complaint I would have is that they usually have a long wait, especially for brunch so come early and be prepared to wait! it's certainly worth it. 

other than that, the atmosphere and food are some
of the best in nashville!

name: Customer_9396
comments:
My friend and I were visiting Nashville and found this place through a quick google search. We were staying downtown, so it was a quick and cheap cab ride away (5 minutes/$7 ride). We went on a Saturday night, so there was about an hour wait. We decided to grab a drink at the bar (no wait there) and stood around chatting/playing a charades game on our phone...which helped pass the time! The drinks were avg. $10/piece. Not cheap, but normal for this kind of restaurant. 

Once we were seated, we knew we wanted to try their french fries (we had previously scoped out the menu) and quickly ordered the sweet potato ones. She ordered the mahi sandwich and I went with the chicken tikka masala, Both were very good.

Would recommend and return!

name: Customer_8884
comments:
Overall: I've only been for brunch and was happy with it soo... nice place to relax and have a little hangover cure on a Saturday or Sunday morning.

Food/Drinks: There are LOTS of brunch options. The Singapore stir fry was great, though it appeared the eggs had been sitting under a heat light for a little while. Still, it was flavorful and not something I've seen anywhere else. I was less impressed with the red velvet waffles. They were extremely dense, and pretty much just tasted like pink waffles. Not bad, just not like red velvet. Be sure to order them with a side of maple syrup, it helps with the density factor. There are a handful of 2fer drink options on the very top of the menu and while they are expensive ($10.50,) from what I've tasted, they're pretty good (and strong.) Go for the blood orange mimosa.

Service/Atmosphere: Our waitress started out being extremely attentive and knowledgeable but kind of dropped off as the meal progressed. That would be understandable if the restaurant had gotten busier but it hadn't. Anyway, she was still nice so I won't complain anymore. The restaurant is very open but seems smaller than when it was under its old name (Lime.) I do like the big open bar, though.

Price: About $40 for 2 people to eat & get a drink a piece for brunch (not including tip)

name: Customer_3253
comments:
This place is awesome!  We stumbled upon it after checking into our hotel...we wanted to walk around after being in the car for 9 hours and we were starving.  We got a table outside, it was loud, but what do you expect on a Friday night in early summer?
The food was great....I got the Nuevo Israeli bread salad and my husband got the turkey blt (with sweet potato chips (YUMMMM)--both fantastic.  
They have an extensive drink/beer list and the staff is knowledgeable about the beer they serve and didn't steer my husband wrong.  
Would recommend trying this place out if you haven't already.

name: Customer_4709
comments: Burger was great. Cooked perfectly, but nothing special. Packed for brunch specials. Seem to have awesome election of cocktails and awesome bartenders. Was there for food, don't really drink. Def would go back. Atmosphere was great too.

name: Customer_3473
comments: We went for lunch today. Service was too slow for anyone on a lunch break (it took nearly an hour). There wasn't a lunch menu, so we paid dinner prices for dinner portions. I saw a little section of "fast plates". I forget what it was called, but none of those items really jumped out at me. We ordered fish tacos, beef tacos with Korean BBQ and fries. It was all good. This might be a better place for dinner.

name: Customer_3574
comments: Good stuff for brunch if you are drinking. Recommend getting there early as it was packed when we got there around 11 and there was a ton of people waiting when we left.

name: Customer_9552
comments: I went to Tavern on a Saturday night and waited about 20 minutes for our table for 2, which really is pretty good! We ordered a few plates to share- egg rolls, fish tacos and Tuscan fries. The egg rolls were served with queso and salsa... for a Chinese food... that was weird. When I've had garlic Parmesan fries in the past, they're usually served with a dipping sauce of some kind, but these were not. We were given a heaping serving of them that 2 of us couldn't finish though. The fish tacos were by far the best dish we had- HIGHLY recommend them! Our waitress was very nice, though it took her quite a few minutes to actually come over to us initially to take drink orders. Other than that she was wonderful. We each ordered a cocktail and they were strong for sure- I was just unimpressed with both. The julep was decent. The second drink was a grapefruit/lemon lime/ vodka drink that tasted like I drank straight grapefruit juice instead of a mixed drink... to be fair, the waitress did ask if I wanted it remade. The ambiance was great, and it was defintely crowded. They had a DJ playing music and it was a younger crowd.

name: Customer_8878
comments: So cute! A must stop on your Nashville adventure!!! Cutest drinks and brunch spot. I got the red sangria and an egg white and fruit brunch. My friends for mimosas. We are all so happy!

name: Customer_5740
comments: I had high hopes after hearing good things and reading good reviews from numerous sites. A friend and I went for brunch and while we waited 45 minutes for a table, that was expected. After being seated our waitress took our drink orders and came back about 5 minutes later with waters and another 10 with my friend's blood orange mimosa. We ordered and waited over an hour for our food. When the waitress finally checked on us I asked about the toast for my son because I knew he was hungry. She came back 10 minutes later with our meal which, to my dismay, was disappointing. I've had better food at a local diner in town and for half the price. I have no idea how long our food sat under heat lamps but my white trash hash was cold and the eggs on the  nooner I ordered were overcooked. My friend ordered the roasted peppers and squashes and said hers was good but she couldn't eat the hash. The service was pretty crummy. We had to ask for our check and then we had to ask the hostess for someone to check us out because our waitress must have forgotten about us. Overall it was a dismal experience and while I was excited to take my husband the next time we are in Nashville, I think we'll be eating elsewhere.

name: Customer_6183
comments: We came here because of all the great yelp reviews, I can't believe this is 4-stars.. Good beer selection, good atmosphere, and decent service.  The food, however, was bla.. We really wanted to try the fried chicken skins, they came out very hard and very stuck together.  The sauce had good flavor but the skins came in a clump that we could hardly break apart. Our food came out about 4 minutes into our attempt to chisel the skins apart. Kaya toast was weird and really lacked anything to bring the dish together.  After scraping off the sauce it was basically Texas toast and an egg.  The 2 sets of tacos we ordered were both overcooked and VERY dry. Come here for drinks, skip the food!

name: Customer_1276
comments: Maybe they gave a great brunch? I had their burger for dinner it was not very good dry with little flavor. Fries were greasy. The service was nice. Valet parking.

name: Customer_5570
comments:
I thought this place was called 'Whiskey Tavern"- That is what the sign said. Its so cool they dropped the Whiskey.  hmm, okay, Tavern it is. Then I kept calling it Whiskey Kitchen because well it is just like Whiskey Kitchen. 

The dark woods, dim light bulbs and limited tables all from IKEAS dark collection, snooty staff, high drink prices and 6 tables on reserved at 5:30 on a Saturday seems a bit weird for a "tavern" 

I went here with a few friends. We just wanted to grab a drink. Even though there were not seats at the bar I proceeded to tell the security-ish hostess we'd just stand and drink our drinks. Seemed like a strange concept to her. We wedged our way in there and was asked if we were waiting for a table. We weren't. The bartender was shocked we were just getting 'drinks'. You won't find a food review here. 

We ordered our drinks and she held her hand out waiting to pay out. No problem. After paying immediately after ordering, we had to drink the drinks.  Lots of huffin and puffin and stink eyes that we were just going to stand there and drink! 

If you like to be 'seen', enjoy bars with chains on the wall, in this room where Tom Edison light bulbs meets LA-tude this is your jam.

name: Customer_7388
comments: Great brunch and cocktails! The Nooner, Roasted Peppers and Squash, and Blueberry Waffles were great. Very good Bloody Mary, red sangria, and signature craft cocktails.

name: Customer_5405
comments: Nice bar with good music and lively atmosphere. The beef Tacos were so Yummy, and so were the fries. Went if there happy

name: Customer_4189
comments: Another Yelper hit it -- this is a noisy, crowded restaurant with big screen TVs.  I wouldn't call it a sports bar.  Nothing wrong with the place.  Cool location, good beer selection.  The food - delicious, but eliminates itself as a "sports bar". My sons and I wanted to catch some pub grub and the hockey game.  Got the game.  The grub-- eclectic.  Do go here if you want a busy, bustling, energetic, tasty, flavorful, thumping music-beat experience.  Don't go here if you want  a burger, a beer and a hockey game amidst sports conversation.

name: Customer_7639
comments:
Good: The food was fantastic. We had a large group (10+) and came here for brunch (and drinks, natch). I had the eggs benedict with short ribs, and loved it. From what I can tell, the rest of the group all enjoyed their dishes as well, from the fried rice breakfast dish to the nachos to the AMAZING peanut butter pancakes. As a starter/side, do not under any circumstances pass up on the "white trash hash" - hasbrowns with white cheddar cheese. YUM.

Bad: The wait was ludicrous. Yes, it was a Saturday, and yes, we had a large group, but Christ Almighty. We waited at the bar (standing room only) for over two hours before being seated. Even if we had split into smaller groups, without a reservation, the wait time would've still been close to an hour and a half. Yikes.

name: Customer_9520
comments: I liked this place a lot, a more refined food/beverage option among a sea of walkable college dive bars. Modern well-designed multi-level interior filled with natural light by day, soft mood lighting at night. Nice looking and well-dressed mixed-age crowd both times I was here. Excellent 2-for-1 Thursday Happy Hour 2-10 PM with a solid selection of pours. This neighborhood likes its drink . . Food reasonably priced and a good mix of options, not perfect, but for essentially up-scale " bar food", it's good.  I bet brunch on weekends here would be fun. My "Ham-Jam-Bread & Butter" was delicious.  Awesome lettuce wraps, at $14.50. Lobster Sliders at twice the price were a letdown, but as in life: Shit happens. Hard working friendly bartenders. I recommend it if you're near Vanderbilt.  Walking distance to many hotels (Courtyard, Hampton Inn, A-Loft, Hilton Garden, The Hutton). A little loud inside, but you're still able to hold a conversation, and the up-tempo music adds to the vibe.

name: Customer_8951
comments:
Lots of good options in this area and the tavern is definitely one of them.  I came here for drinks one night and lunch during the day.   A bit of a wait for dinner so make sure you get a reservation if you can.

We got an appetizer - buffalo cauliflower.  It's slightly breaded and engulfed in buffalo sauce.  Good taste, but would've preferred to have it a bit crispier.  

Ordered the burger - cooked medium, lettuce, tomato, American (cheese is extra).  The fries were okay - comes in a little fryer basket.  The burger had a good sear on the outside and properly seasoned with salt.  

Good spot for food and drinks.

name: Customer_3959
comments: The atmosphere is very nice. I always am leery of "hipster" spots but this place is legit. Super friendly and not pretentious staff. Female bartender made one of the best Bulleit neat Old Fashioned's I've had out. Other mixed drinks were also prepared well (well balanced without being boozy). I ordered Korean beef tacos. They were not bad but not one of my favorites either. They were still good. The table over got nachos that looked delicious. I also think if a place has a clean bathroom, their kitchen is usually clean too. This place is spotless. I also was impressed to see the bartenders cleaning bottles and the bar in their down time. Overall, I would definitely visit again when I am in town. I'd actually rate this place a 4.5 stars if I could.

name: Customer_1095
comments: A friend recommended this restaurant to me while on a business trip to Nashville. The food and service were great! It's a really cool atmosphere with lots of fresh air. Unique menu items, and everything that I saw come out looked so good.

name: Customer_2478
comments:
The simply-named Tavern offers up some mighty simple comfort food pleasures (White Trash hash, anyone?) and elevated junk food game bites. 

That said, I'm not sure this is quite the weekend brunch place for me, due to the TVs providing all of the background noise. I'm not a fan of big TVs blaring games -- to me, this is the worst kind of ambiance. BUT... for those of you seeking a place to watch local sports and cheer on with a crowd, Tavern is the spot for you, especially if your tastes are a bit more high brow than your typical nachos. I mean, they have nachos, but Tavern's come with pistachio and goat cheese. Nice! 

I'd easily return on a non game day (or even to sit on the shaded side patio) for more of that White Trash Hash. Think tater tot casserole. I mean, really. Goodbye hangover. The egg white omelet I had was kinda blah, as the tomatoes made it seem extra watery.The "Wicked" Bloody Mary was hardly wicked, more like gentle, despite the vodka being infused with pickled things that you'd hope for on your glass. They don't automatically garnish the way you'd think. Or at least the way a New Orleanian would think. I mean... just a lime? Nu uh. Our very lovely server came out with some olives for us, which was nice. But a Bloody without beaucoup d' garnish is a naked Mary, indeed.

Extra props for three bottles of hot sauces on the table, marked X, XX and XXX. Go for the orangey habanero, as it's the tastiest of the bunch (it might be the XX). Don't be fooled by the warnings. They are there for the bland American palate.

name: Customer_2222
comments: So cute! A must stop on your Nashville adventure!!! Cutest drinks and brunch spot. I got the red sangria and an egg white and fruit brunch. My friends for mimosas. We are all so happy!

name: Customer_7599
comments: I literally had the best grilled salmon of my life here! This place is amazing. The food is extremely good. My husband had chimichanga and he is also very happy  with his food. The service was great too. I can't recommend this place more!

name: Customer_6476
comments:
We totally blew off all Nashville brunch recommendations just because the menu at Tavern looked so good.  Risky move, bucking the suggestions of former residents and frequent visitors, but I'm happy to report it paid off handsomely.  

I looove the set-up of the restaurant.  There's a covered/open air area, a bar area with some booths and high-top tables, then a cozy area "upstairs" overlooking the action so to speak.  It basically has a seating location for whatever your mood.  Very cool.

The brunch menu was almost impossible to choose from.  Our eyes went directly to the red velvet waffle with cream cheese drizzle.  We're not big sweets for breakfast folks but we do love our desserts.  But the inevitable was sure to occur, eat brunch and be too full - rule of thumb - order your sweets at the same time as your meal if you're determined to try something.  So we did....

I opted for the benedict uno which was fantastic.  Tender braised short ribs on an english muffin with perfectly cooked poached eggs and a Tabasco hollandaise.  Soooo incredibly good and the hollandaise was the perfect combination of buttery and spicy.  Excellent.  I will say, if you don't love hollandaise you would be put off - my plate was literally swimming in sauce (arm floaties and all...)  I gobbled it up but it turned my wife off from trying it (note to self, don't bath in hollandaise.)

My wife opted for the The Nooner which is an omelet with bacon, fried oysters and a
spicy sour cream, served with "white trash hash" (basically a heavily hashbrown casserole.)   So back to the red velvet wafftle....we didn't finish it....I know...I know....we tried and we did a pretty good job, but we just couldn't.  It was super good although almost not quite done in the middle, but tasty nonetheless.  

Good service, good food, great atmosphere (would love to watch a game here and snack my way through the day.)  Can't wait to return!

name: Customer_5811
comments: I could eat the blue cheese fondue on almost anything. I bet liver would taste good in that fondue. Fortunately I had some really good buffalo cauliflower to go along with and I hasten to say it was a top 5 all time appetizer ever.People rave about the fries and they were good but not the best I have had. The Tavern burger on the other-hand may be the best burger I have ever had. Made from ground rib-eye and filet makes me believe God made the burger lol The lobster sliders were really good but 22 bucks not that good. The mushroom soup had to be made by Angels it was amazing. Its a little pricey but you definitely get what you pay for, for the most part. As a whole it may be the best lunch ever. I give very few 5 stars on average and this was well earned. The place is nice and cozy and the staff were great. It was a religious experience involving food.

name: Customer_1047
comments:
My husband and I enjoyed a late meal here last night (Monday). It wasn't too crowded, but filled up before we left. 

We sat on the patio and enjoyed the warm Nashville night.

My husband ordered the bucket of mussels and I had the beef short rib tacos.

The tacos are small, so if you're hungry, order three! It was perfect for me, though. The meat was tender and delicious. It had sliced cucumber and a spicy sauce which was to die for. 

The bucket of mussels was a large portion of mussels in a broth, served with a large chunk of french bread for dipping.  My husband enjoyed them to the end. I asked if they had a lot of garlic and he said not at all. He was delighted with the light sauce.

Although our waitress, Jennifer, who might just be the best waitress in the world, suggested many desserts (including s'mores, which involved bringing a little fire pit to the table with hershey's chocolate, strawberries and reeses) we opted for the reverse root beer float: root beer gelato with creme soda over the top. It was delicious! (Had I been out with the girlfriends, we definitely would have tried the s'mores..next time!)

As I said, Jennifer, our waitress was very attentive. She knew in detail about every item on the menu (as we ask a lot of questions!) and took great care of us.

We would definitely recommend this restaurant to any one in the area.

name: Customer_1815
comments: Went to lunch at Tavern today 8/29/17 with three co-workers who had never been before on my recommendation. It was a huge mistake on my part. Tavern had been ok on previous visits but today a real disappointment. Slow and indifferent service. Hidden costs-charges for extra salsa on already over priced nachos. Ordered extra chicken on the nachos- it was not on the nachos when they arrived-we were still charged for them because Tavern brought us a plate of luke warm chicken to pour on after we'd already finished. We asked about the hidden cost of the chicken and salsa our server rolled her eyes and let us know she does not make the rules. This place is way overrated, over priced and the douche bag factor is off the charts. Fu*k Tavern.

name: Customer_8526
comments: Go for the buffalo cauliflower! What better combination could you ask for?! The drinks also are delicious. The space is large and draws a mix after work - a great place for happy hour.

name: Customer_7113
comments: Got to the restaraunt and gave the name under our reservation. They don't take reservations and don't know why open table lists them but they get that a lot. Hmm ok. Can you try to do something for us since it isn't our fault you haven't contacted open table? No, 1 hr wait. No problem, we will go next door for drinks. Get text from resturant that let's you check status through wait for out....opentable. Hmmmm. Come back in an hr, get seated outside even though there are plenty of spaces inside. Fine. Drink wifey ordered was the best part of the experince. Can we order the cauliflower - no, we are out of our most popular item. Ok. Guac appetizer - made from half an avocado and a thousand chips. $12 Salad with ahi - 1 dimensional salad with 3 pieces of ahi. Ahi was good wish there was more of it. Salad had no diversity anything interesting $23 Chicken kabobs - supposed to be with ginger terriyaki and sesame and garlic. Only thing I could taste was terriyaki, very heavy handed. Nothing we ordered was beyond marginal...

name: Customer_2789
comments: Came here during a recent trip to Nashville. Came here a couple years ago for brunch which was amazing but a super long wait so beware. Didn't realize when I picked this place this time that they also do a 2 for 1 drink special from 2-10pm on Wednesday nights. This is a great deal but makes the night a lot busier. I was with an older group of people so they personally didn't like how much noise was going on in the restaurant. In terms of food I do feel like it's a little overpriced for what you get. But I will say the mahi-mahi tacos were tasty. I would definitely come back on future trips to Nashville. And if they take reservations I will do that instead.

name: Customer_1714
comments: Food and service was great! Try the BLT and the egg rolls! The drinks are so good as well.

name: Customer_9550
comments: Delicious brunch, fabulous service! The buy one get one brunch drinks were a plus! It started getting crowded at 11am, so I suggest getting there when they open at 10am!

name: Customer_2158
comments: We came here based off a recommendation from our hotel.  The food was fine but nothing impressive.  It was basic bar food.  The music was way too loud.  Impossible to have a conversation and we were there at 5:30 on a Saturday.  If you're in from out of town, try another place for dinner.

name: Customer_7607
comments: We came here because of all the great yelp reviews, I can't believe this is 4-stars.. Good beer selection, good atmosphere, and decent service.  The food, however, was bla.. We really wanted to try the fried chicken skins, they came out very hard and very stuck together.  The sauce had good flavor but the skins came in a clump that we could hardly break apart. Our food came out about 4 minutes into our attempt to chisel the skins apart. Kaya toast was weird and really lacked anything to bring the dish together.  After scraping off the sauce it was basically Texas toast and an egg.  The 2 sets of tacos we ordered were both overcooked and VERY dry. Come here for drinks, skip the food!

name: Customer_4964
comments: Meet by a great hostess at the door, Jenna. Her smile was amazing! Drinks at the bar were rather good.  They actually have a loco moco! BOOM!

name: Customer_1637
comments: You find yourself in an unfamiliar city, it's raining, and you need to duck in somewhere. You choose Tavern Midtown. The ambiance is modern rustic. Great music, and knowledgeable, friendly bartenders await. Per recommendation, I decided on the Tavern Burger and fries. For more detail, ribeye & filet beef blend with a perfectly toasted bun, two slices of red onion, thick cut tomato, four evenly cut pickle chips, two slices of bacon, and three roasted green chilis. Perfectly cooked throughout, it is the perfect dinner to satisfy the palate during this business trip. The Belgian fries are not too soggy, not overly salted. As good served with roasted garlic aioli as they are with the Louisiana XX hot sauce. Food: 5/5 Ambiance: 4/5 Staff: 5/5 Come back factor: 6/5 Thank you for a great experience!

name: Customer_6208
comments:
Was in Nashville this past weekend with some friends. Decided to try this place as it was close to where we were staying. 

The place is very quaint on the inside. Dark lighting, the type of spot that could suffice a first date, a work event or a family get together. My friend and I showed up around 3pm and strangely there was a ten minute wait (Which is weird, because it's that awkward time in between lunch and dinner, but whatever.) 

Our server is super friendly and attentive. I order the pan seared tuna with a side of the sweet potato fries with jalapeno ketchup. My friend orders the tavern burger. 

Our food comes. I take a bite of my tuna and it appears raw, almost entirely uncooked. I try again and can't bare it. The waiter has no problem swapping my order for the salmon which is very kind of him. My friend appears to enjoy the burger. The fries are fine-- not seven dollar side worthy fine, but decent enough. The jalapeno ketchup tastes like regular ketchup. The salmon doesn't particularly taste like fish (almost like an overly marinated chicken, which wouldn't be a bad thing if it wasn't brought under the guise of fish) but I run through it because I'm starved. We pay and the meal for me was at its best below average. Especially for the cost. 

Naturally the evening/early morning hits and I've got all types of food poisoning and stomach bug type issues (diarrhea, nauseous, headache, puking.) This was Monday morning/ Sunday evening. It's now Thursday and I'm still ill. Not quite sure how these people are cleaning their meats, but I won't be back anytime soon. Nice, attentive staff and sweet vibe. Food was awful.

name: Customer_6967
comments: Absolutely awesome menu, the beer selection was fantastic and most importantly, Emily did a fantastic job taking care of us. I had the pork chop and loved it!  Others at the table had the chimichanga, the Son of a Brown Bag and the Loco, all very well reviewed. Highly recommend this place that's in a great area of town.

name: Customer_6070
comments: I have never been so insulted and talked down to in my life. Michelle, I think that's her name it's on my receipt but she never introduced herself, was the rudest person I have ever given my money to in my life. When we sat down she was talking about personal issues with the barback loud enough for us to hear and I thought that was odd in and off itself. When she gave us our menus she said a few times "these menus are good for the next 30 seconds."  Sorry but either give us brunch or give us dinner menus and explain that the kitchen is in the midst of a shift change, don't make us feel pressured because you dropped menus that have an extremely short time limit. Instead of eating we decided to just get drinks. She let us know that the brunch menu libations were, her words, 2 for 1. We ordered a mimosa off the list and hung out. When we got get drinks they set two wooden tokens down but didn't reference the at all, so we didn't know what they were for.  Eventually ordered some food off the dinner menu to go. She was very non existent the whole time we were sitting at the bar, not attentive at all. When we asked for the bill I saw that both our drinks were on there. I asked about them and let her know about the 2 for 1 statement she said. She then proceeded to tell me it was buy one, get one and that's what the tokens are for. I told her that "buy one get one" and "2 for 1" are different and if we knew it was BOGO we would have ordered another drink (if she would have even paid attention to us).  After a little back and forth she said she would take care of it and that "they weren't trying to screw us."  She talked to us like we were the worst people on earth because she doesn't know how to explain her own restaurants policies. I work in an industry that has me visiting 10-15 bars/restaurants/hotels a day and I have never had a worse hospitality experience in my life. Tavern Management - this employee is losing you revenue left and right.  Not only is she not taking care of customers and grabbing reorders, she is turning people away for good. This treatment was so horrible and off putting that I am going to go out of my way to recommended against going to Tavern due to the disrespect we felt. Hopefully your floor managers recognize how bad she is and theyo do something about it because she is taking money out of your pocket every shift she works.

name: Customer_1312
comments: Drinks were strong! Guacamole and fries were excellent. Beef short rib tacos were like chewing on a tire. Mahi sandwich was overcooked and super fishy. Tried this place a few years ago, never came back but thought we would give it another shot. Probably won't be back, maybe for guacamole and fries. Our server was awesome though.

name: Customer_3755
comments: My husband and I are visiting Nashville from Chicago (go cubs). We have been to tavern once before last year and my husband fell in love with the chickenooga drink. So in love that tavern was our first stop back in town. Well, one chickenooga into the night and there was an issue with the keg equipment making this drink unavailable. The manager soon came over with a substitute option replacing the beer. They very well could have just said "too bad" but went way above and beyond and made my husband content. Great food too but the service is well above the rest!

name: Customer_6567
comments: Food was just about ok. Service very average and slow. Also, charging extra for something as simple as soy sauce is a bit strange when their other condiments were complimentary. Bar staff was good though.

name: Customer_4133
comments:
So my girlfriend and I wanted to have a low key night. We went in around 8pmon a Friday night and the wait to get a table was about an hour. 

We decided to go to the bar and have a drink while we waited. 
A spot at the bar came open, so we took that instead.  Good thing, because almost 2 hours in,  they still wouldn't have called our name?

At first I loved the crowd.  It was a tad older.  It was a nice "after work" 30 something crowd. NONE of the local "socialites" were there.  However as midnight approached, that changed. It turned into the Virago/Whiskey Kitchen crowd.  Which I know many people don't go to WK for that very reason.  

Onto food and drink.  I had the Nacho's and my friend had the fried fish.  Neither one of us were the least bit impressed with the food. She said her's was very bland and mine was not impressive at all. However she did give props to the spicy ketchup that comes with the fries!   

As for our drinks.  Fancy names and high prices sum it up. I was brave and tried the "preserves" drink.  I went with Gin and the pinapple and honey preserves .. i think that is what it was.  
It was very strong.  The bartender told me that it would start to taste different with time. Um, no.   It tasted like gin with a little jelly.  I don't care how "new york" and trendy it is suppose to be (that is how it was described to me) it was gross. 

It was nice. A bigger Whiskey Kitchen is the best way to describe it. 
I'm sure I'll go back, but I will stick with drinks I know and try to leave before the pretentious crowd arrives. 

One other note.  The manager kept coming over to us numerous times to make sure we were happy.  I though that was nice!

name: Customer_4542
comments: I like Tavern a lot. The food is very good. I went here for lunch with a friend from work. I loved the vibe, the dim-ish lighting, and the music, and would definitely like to come back at night time. The fish was very good, fresh, and the batter was light and perfect. I loved the sauces that came with my meal. I shouldn't have gotten the sweet potato fries. Didn't care for them. Next time I'll get regular ones. Also loved the fact that they have all of those hot sauces at the table. Any place with an abundance of hot sauces is awesome to me. I would like to go back and try other food. The only negative thing was it took far too long to eat here on our lunch break. The service was very slow, but maybe the server was new. We had an hour break and we are late coming back. However, will go back again, definitely.

name: Customer_1514
comments: We came here because of all the great yelp reviews, I can't believe this is 4-stars.. Good beer selection, good atmosphere, and decent service.  The food, however, was bla.. We really wanted to try the fried chicken skins, they came out very hard and very stuck together.  The sauce had good flavor but the skins came in a clump that we could hardly break apart. Our food came out about 4 minutes into our attempt to chisel the skins apart. Kaya toast was weird and really lacked anything to bring the dish together.  After scraping off the sauce it was basically Texas toast and an egg.  The 2 sets of tacos we ordered were both overcooked and VERY dry. Come here for drinks, skip the food!

name: Customer_2536
comments: We came here based off a recommendation from our hotel.  The food was fine but nothing impressive.  It was basic bar food.  The music was way too loud.  Impossible to have a conversation and we were there at 5:30 on a Saturday.  If you're in from out of town, try another place for dinner.

name: Customer_1748
comments:
I really enjoyed my mussels and the atmosphere in Tavern, but this place wasn't the homerun I expected. We had a 20 minute wait on a game day, so I thought that was very reasonable. Tavern has a ton of TVs, so it's great for watching a game. The bartenders were pretty quick to provide drinks as we waited, and the craft brew and cocktail menu is good. There isn't a very expansive selection, but what's available is diverse. The food is pretty stellar as well. My mussels were delicious and our nacho appetizer was great without any meat. Fresh jalapeños, black beans, and the perfect amount of cheese made them a delight. Our server is what missed the mark. She was courteous for sure, but her timing was really off. It took a while for us to order once seated and she altered between smothering us or ignoring the table. I also wasn't impressed with my friends' lamb tacos. The tacos come in an order of two or three, and this place seems to be stingy with the meat filling. I'd definitely recommend a side an order of three. 

All and all, I'd come back. This place is tasty, but it's not the pinnacle of dining.

name: Customer_8511
comments:
If you think you are walking into a typical bar menu .... think again!  Wonderful, original recipes.  I had a kale salad, guacamole and chicken wings.  All awesome with non conventional ingredients (finally chopped kale with parmesan cheese, nuts, lemon).  Guacamole with pistachio nuts and goat cheese!  Who would have thought!!

Really good!

name: Customer_1181
comments: What a fabulous new place to dine! The staff is extremely friendly, the food is creative and they have the BEST burger in town! Not only is the food great, but their use of social media is as well. I sent a tweet out about how great their burger is and received a nice card and gift certificate for my next dining experience. Nicely done, guys!

name: Customer_4008
comments:
The food here is outstanding. I generally get the Tavern Burger, which is legitimately one of the best in town. The desserts are great as well; for instance, they let you make s'mores at your table. Furthermore, the beer selection is fairly robust, usually with several local breweries on tap. 

The downside here is the service. First, it's usually quite slow, even when the dining room is not too busy. It's taken over an hour to get my lunch before, and not during peak hours. However, the pace does not bother me as much as some of the staff's snooty demeanor. The hostesses in particular are generally a bit condescending, which is off-putting. The wait staff themselves are usually a bit better; you can tell they work for tips, whereas the hostesses quite clearly do not. All in all a good spot for lunch or supper, though.

name: Customer_4060
comments: Great place to grab drinks with friends! The waitresses were super friendly. Go on Thursday nights for the best drink specials. One con is that the food isn't that great, but this place is fabulous for drinks.

name: Customer_9863
comments: After drinking a few glasses of 1920 (the best cocktail in Nashville if you ask me), I am the happiest girl around! I also love the menu, it's fun without being weird. I can't stop eating the Philly cheesesteak eggrolls, brown bag special, all the different fries, and the kale salad.

name: Customer_6480
comments: After a failed attempt at a much busier and more popular restaurant nearby, we found the Tavern to be the perfect spot to start off our Nashville trip. There was no wait on a Friday night around 11pm. We were starving and impatient for something satisfyingly unhealthy and deliciuos. The two of us definately over-ordered. After we received our beer and cider orders, we placed our gargantuan order for two: the Tuscan style Tavern fries, which was HUGE, the chips and guacamole and the fish and chips. Obviously, the healthy factor was not an issue. Everything was tasty, just in huge portions. The Tavern fries were easy to munch on, although there was way too much. We probably could have ordered this alone. But I guess if an order of fries cost $6.50, I wouldn't expect just a small tin. The guacamole was interesting. The goat cheese gave it a different flavor - but I liked it. There were so many chips but at the same time, there was a lot of guac. The fish and chips wasn't bad, not mind blowing either. It was so greasy I could only take several bites before calling it quits. I love when my fried fish is super tender and juicy, but this was a bit much. When each bite you take the grease seems to flow out into your mouth, it may be too much. Overall, a delicious late night meal for ones who were unable to wait 45 minutes for a table at 9:30pm elsewhere... I'd defintely come back here for a couple beers and an order of their Tavern fries.

name: Customer_4048
comments: I at least have to give this restaurant two stars due to the decent food. But while on a dinner meeting and after spending $100 on entrées and appetizers, I had to flag down the assistant cook, (the guy in bright red baggy pants watching TV), to see if I could get more avocado for my tuna entrée.  He made it very apparent and direct that he could not help me with that situation and I would have to flag down my  waitress so she could bill me for the four dollar avocado.

name: Customer_4783
comments:
I waited a couple days before rating to try to be fair. This place was recommended and hyped separately to me and my husband in transit and upon arrival to Nashville. We expected a lot. 
The service was great. We sat at the bar, both bartenders and food service were polite and attentive. Drink selection and quality and price seemed good. The food is another story. It is over priced and over hyped by reviewers.
My husband had the OZ pot pie. Even with a healthy dose of the curry sauce, it was dry. And plain, could barely taste the curry. I had korean short rib tacos. Nothing korean about them. I tasted sriracha and soy sauce. Isn't  Korean about gochujang? Meat was dry.  The fries are house cut, plentiful and phenomenal. But the rest of the menu is overpriced ignorance.

name: Customer_8591
comments: Truly not worth the wait. I've tried a couple dishes and nothing has been great- wouldn't really recommend. Almost everything I have tried has either been too dry or too salty. The ambiance is nice but it's pretty slow. The only good food item is their fries.

name: Customer_2488
comments: Solid brunch spot! Got there at peak time and the wait was less than what they thought. In the interim we sat on the padded benches outside. The place was packed but they seemed to turn it over and get people in and out quick. The bazooka guacamole was very good but the star of the show was the chorizo gravy on the biscuits. The spicy chicken sausage is aptly named as it packs a punch. I love hot food so it was perfect for me. My fiancé said it was at the limit of her spice scale so normal people may find it too much. She has the pretzel pancakes which are pancakes with pretzels on top covered in syrup. It wasn't what we expected but was good. Something about biting into a pretzel and it not having any crunch doesn't feel right but that may just be us. The girl with us had the pain Perdu and couldn't finish it but said it was good. We will for sure make our way back here as we each tried to decide between 3 different dishes so I look forward to having tried them all.

name: Customer_3800
comments: Well, the concept seems cool....but, not great service.  The waitress forgot our drinks - we has finished our appetizer and they had not arrived, so we cancelled them. We tried to order 1 of the 3 late night dinner entrees they offered, but they were all out.  Umm, bummer. We left and I don't think we will be back.

name: Customer_3743
comments: I was so disappointed that my 2nd Tavern experince wasn't as flawless as my first one. I'm only giving it 3 stars due to the service we received from the manager and because most of the food was still good. I met 3 friends for a late Saturday brunch, 2 of which had never been there before. I was excited to introduce them to Tavern's fabulousness but left feeling a little embarrassed after the service we received. For starters, it took about 20 minutes before our server even acknowledged us. I asked about drink specials and as soon as the last word came out of her mouth she walked away leaving me unable to order a drink. About 10 minutes later she finally came back. After ordering drinks it took another 10 minutes to get them. We were ready to order our meals (had been for about 30 minutes) but again, she walked away before we could do so. Instead, she sauntered on over to the bar and proceeded to talk and flirt with some guy at the bar for over 20 minutes. We timed it. At that point we were so disgusted that we stopped another server walking by and asked if we could order with her. She was happy to help us. My 3 friends ordered the Tavern burger and they all liked it. I opted for a ham and brie omelette and it was kind of meh. I remembered I don't like brie (my fault for ordering it) and I had to pick it all out. The omelette was lacking flavor anyway. I should have at least salt and peppered it myself, I guess. The side of white trash hash was very tasty but an extremely small serving. Only about 5 bites. Because of our shitty server we were never offered to order a second round of drinks and it was past happy hour since of course we had been sitting at the table for almost 2 hours at that point. Dirty dishes sat on our table for 30 minutes while we waited for our checks. During our 2 hours at the table our server only came around 3 times. Very disappointing. With the exception of the burgers my friends had, the dining experience was pretty terrible. We ended up speaking with Madeline, the manager, about our experience. She was very nice and seemed to sincerely care about what we had to say. She ended up comping our entire meal and gave us some coupons to come back and try brunch again. However, while we were speaking with Madeline the server in question was whispering and giggling with a busboy and staring at our table. Our point of "complaining" was truly not to get anything free, but to let these little brats know that people aren't just going to stand by and let them slack on their job while they run around and socialize. We ended up tipping the server who actually took our order. I'm hoping this horrible expereince was just a fluke because I really like Tavern and want to continue coming back.

name: Customer_3445
comments:
Food is great, drinks are great, deals are great (Brunch with 2-4-1 drinks? Heck yeah!). The menu is extensive and interesting, with unique twists on classic dishes. The service is also great, but I am withholding a fifth star due to the management's seating policies.

We came for brunch on a Sunday expecting an hour plus wait, so when the hostess informed us it would be 1hr45m we weren't surprised. However, we became frustrated when we noticed there were 4 open tables on the patio that still hadn't been seated after an hour of waiting. It was a beautiful day so we asked the hostess about it and she said that the tables were reserved. When we asked again, she explained that the patio tables were not assigned to a specific server but were instead added on to a server's load inside, so they weren't seating them because they didn't want to overwhelm the servers. Totally understandable to not want to overwork your servers, but why not seat people with the caveat that service will be slower? Or better yet, why not specifically assign a server to the outdoor section so that wait times will be lower? Having worked in the service industry, our group was confused by this. We ended up just sitting at one of the empty patio tables until the hostess notified us that a table was ready. 

We ordered the Cheddar Biscuit, the Wood Fire Double Yokes, and a Turkey Feta Omelette from the specials board and all were delicious. The biscuit comes in a trio and though it doesn't look like a lot of food they are VERY filling. Our server surprised us with a side of White Trash Hash on the house because our food was taking longer than expected (we didn't even notice the timing, so it was a very nice gesture). The White Trash Hash is a must, this stuff is addicting! Potatoes, rice, and gooey cheese- who could ask for more.

Overall, great place for brunch in Nashville. Expect a long line but food worth the wait. Hopefully management can improve their seating policies to cut down on wait times in the future.

name: Customer_3083
comments:
My favorite place to eat and/or drink in Nashville.  

It's in midtown, which is local and away from the honky tonks.  The ambiance, food, drinks, and service is great.  And if anything, there is always good people watching.  I come to Tavern after church for brunch, out with my girlfriends for drinks, or out to a nice fun dinner with my boyfriend. 

My birthday was on a Wednesday last year, which is 2-for-1's night. I came with my girlfriends and had my favorite dessert, their S'mores!  So much fun!

When asked where do I want to go for brunch? Lunch? Dinner? or just a night out...I always pick Tavern.

name: Customer_7670
comments:
Great staff, service and food!

I ordered the kale salad (OMGosh - good!), short ribs tacos and the fried cauliflower- a MUST - even if you don't finish it all.

name: Customer_4781
comments:
Unfortunately they don't take reservations.  It was a crazy busy weekend and took about an hour to be seated.
Sat on porch behind bar, they had propane heaters so it was plenty warm despite 15 degree weather.
Service was very attentive and friendly.  Food was great. Shasito peppers were perfect. Cauliflower was good and smoking hot spicy.
Glad we waited.

name: Customer_9802
comments:
Not my cuppa gin. Probably because of all that basil.

Tavern is big, a bit brash, bro-friendly with all the TVs and reasonably priced for its prime location on Broadway. Drop your name and cell phone number at the host stand and get sexted when your table is ready. So tech.

Reviews sing praises of their prime beef burgers, so wifey and I opted for a pair, each with bacon and cheese. Subbing a side salad for fries comes with a surcharge... the amount will totally surprise you. (Clickbait header fail: It's $3.50.)

With the fixin's and the greens, a $9.50 patty sizzled up to $16. And the lasting impression is nil, save the need for seasoning and a Maillard crust. It's an average burger that should be $8 at any pub, which gives me pause as to why it comes so highly praised. An off-night in the kitchen? Labor Day weekend lethargy? Unclear. The end result just didn't resonate.

Could cocktails save the day? Her berry julep was all pulp and my 1920 (a gin, grapefruit, ginger and basil concoction borrowed from Brinkley's) tasted only of the green leaf. No tartness, no ginger bite, no other herbal subtleties from the spirit. Just basil. All the basil. At least they were cheap-ish!

comments: Hmmmmm it's decent. Not sure about the 'rave' reviews to be honest. The prices kind of turned me off. They have a brunch item of Kaya Toast which is to out it bluntly ridiculously overpriced. I can get a jar of Kaya from the Asian market for 1/10the price of the dish. Not impressed.
