Awesome atmosphere with a brunch of tvs. Can be a little loud though.

name: Customer_9802
comments: Overpriced. That's the best way to describe it. Everything was FINE. Just fine. But when our bar tab is $60 for a few drinks, and I felt like I needed to go over the menu about 8 times to find something exciting to try (I landed on the burger), I felt let down. All of the reviews of this place made me want to come visit. I think these must all be Vandy kids or tourists who don't know where the better quality places are with better prices. I just felt, well... so meh about the whole thing. Again, everything was fine, decent, even. But by the time to pay the bill came, my husband and I thought of at LEAST 5 or 6 different places we could have gone for BETTER drinks with CHEAPER prices and a much better menu. Obviously, this is probably for the hip crowd. So, if you're hip, go for it. If you were once hip, and you know better... be prepared to be underwhelmed.

name: Customer_5006
comments: I could eat the blue cheese fondue on almost anything. I bet liver would taste good in that fondue. Fortunately I had some really good buffalo cauliflower to go along with and I hasten to say it was a top 5 all time appetizer ever.People rave about the fries and they were good but not the best I have had. The Tavern burger on the other-hand may be the best burger I have ever had. Made from ground rib-eye and filet makes me believe God made the burger lol The lobster sliders were really good but 22 bucks not that good. The mushroom soup had to be made by Angels it was amazing. Its a little pricey but you definitely get what you pay for, for the most part. As a whole it may be the best lunch ever. I give very few 5 stars on average and this was well earned. The place is nice and cozy and the staff were great. It was a religious experience involving food.

name: Customer_2945
comments: Went today with a group for brunch. We had no complaints. Great-cucumber Bloody Mary, coffee, lobster gumbo, grilled artichoke, white trash hash and service. The decor was tasteful and semi modern. I definitely felt like we left Nashville for a couple hours which was great! Will definitely be back!

name: Customer_8145
comments: Another brunch gem for Midtown! We went here to try a local place before we headed home and we were not disappointed! We started out with the White Trash Hash- holy smokes. They're basically cheesy potatoes but way better. I had the Pretzel Pancakes for my meal and they were the perfect flavor. They were drizzled with dulce de leche and served with a side of white chocolate mousse and they were so good! I also had a side of Texas toast (hello carb day). Ask for the coconut jam with it... UNREAL. My boyfriend had the biscuits with chorizo gravy and he said they were really good. He also asked for a hot chocolate. Our server (I can't remember what her name was but we were in the room that looks out onto the patio on Sunday 12/17) went to the back to check if they had it and it turns out she made it by heating up milk and melting chocolate.. they didn't have packets so she went above and beyond. Incredible food, incredible service, and definitely one of our new regular spots when we visit!

name: Customer_2047
comments: Best brunch! Came here on a busy Saturday with a group of girls. Everyone loved their food and drinks! Waitress was friendly, efficient and knowledgeable about all menu and drink items. Would definitely come here again.

name: Customer_2847
comments:
All around nice upper scale bar.  Exactly what you would expect from a place like this.

Tip:  Get the Kale salad, even as a side.  It's amazing.

name: Customer_8315
comments: First and foremost, this place is worth the wait. If you are planning to eat here, and didn't come before opening, expect at least a 20-30 minute wait if you're lucky. We got here right when the doors opened and only had to wait 20 minutes to get seated. The food is everything it's hyped up to be, and the service was really great. So, as said earlier, this place is worth the wait.

name: Customer_3635
comments: Awesome! Great food, great service! Our waitress Rebecca was wonderful! The Moco Loco was amazing!

name: Customer_7918
comments: I do not unjustly dole out bad reviews, however, i feel it my moral obligation to society to inform the masses of what lies within at tavern... i want to like this place, which took the spot formerly occupied by Lime, but after 3 visits i am left with the same impression: the best thing about this place is it's location/outdoor bar seating.  terrible mixed drinks ... (drink #1: facial toner, drink #2: salad dressing, drink #3: cough syrup)... definitely stick with beer or wine here. the food was ok. i had the turkey sandwich on pretzel bread and sweet potato fries - both were meh (and cold). food was much better when they first opened. sad when standards drop...   (i also had to valet park. then valet disappeared...  my keys ended up behind the bar. that's apparently where they keep them, incase you're looking. or still waiting for your keys.)

name: Customer_4222
comments: Great food!! Everything we ordered was good. Wait was long for Saturday brunch. My fave were the red velvet waffle and Singapore eggs.

name: Customer_1760
comments: Food was fantastic, servic was so bad I wouldn't come back. They are severely understaffed, we finished eating 45 mins before we got the check. The hour and a half wait is completely unnecessary!

name: Customer_8081
comments: A good place. Kind of on the loud side, but a nice place. Fried chicken skins were superior. Rest of food was good and waitress was fairly attentive and kind of tuned in. Not a place to go if you're in a hurry.

name: Customer_4339
comments:
I thought this place was called 'Whiskey Tavern"- That is what the sign said. Its so cool they dropped the Whiskey.  hmm, okay, Tavern it is. Then I kept calling it Whiskey Kitchen because well it is just like Whiskey Kitchen. 

The dark woods, dim light bulbs and limited tables all from IKEAS dark collection, snooty staff, high drink prices and 6 tables on reserved at 5:30 on a Saturday seems a bit weird for a "tavern" 

I went here with a few friends. We just wanted to grab a drink. Even though there were not seats at the bar I proceeded to tell the security-ish hostess we'd just stand and drink our drinks. Seemed like a strange concept to her. We wedged our way in there and was asked if we were waiting for a table. We weren't. The bartender was shocked we were just getting 'drinks'. You won't find a food review here. 

We ordered our drinks and she held her hand out waiting to pay out. No problem. After paying immediately after ordering, we had to drink the drinks.  Lots of huffin and puffin and stink eyes that we were just going to stand there and drink! 

If you like to be 'seen', enjoy bars with chains on the wall, in this room where Tom Edison light bulbs meets LA-tude this is your jam.

name: Customer_9885
comments: Amazing food, great service! Melissa was so accommodating! We got seated right away too.

name: Customer_5992
comments: The atmosphere is very clean, modern, and slightly upscale. They offer a brunch and a large selection of drinks. They are very packed for brunch though. Their brunch runs pretty late. I got there around 2pm and they said brunch was ending soon. Their brunch menu items cost around $10 each. Their normal dinner menu gets a little pricier, but you don't have to spend a lot of money here.

name: Customer_3569
comments: Great place. Good food. Good prices, $30 for 2 people.  Good service. Too loud on the inside but perfect for sitting outside. Try the pretzel sandwich with fries.

name: Customer_9324
comments:
I finally got to come and experience brunch here! Which is easier said than done. I've attempted to come before and the wait was around 1.5-2 hours. 
On Sunday we came around 1115 for a 45 minute wait which wasn't bad for a group of 5. 
It's two for ones for Sunday brunch and I tried the sangria and the blood orange mimosa. I preferred the sangria hands down!
For food I ordered the huevos rancheros which was pretty good. My gf ordered the Singapore stiryfry and the white trash hash and I liked her stir fry a lot!
I will be back for sure because I keep hearing how good the tavern burger is and I won't make the mistake of not ordering it next time! 
Awesome atmosphere with a brunch of tvs. Can be a little loud though.

name: Customer_2037
comments:
Got to the restaurant and gave the name under our reservation. They don't take reservations and don't know why open table lists them but they get that a lot. Hmm ok. Can you try to do something for us since it isn't our fault you haven't contacted open table? No, 1 hr wait. No problem, we will go next door for drinks. Get text from restaurant that let's you check status through wait for out....opentable. Hmmmm.  Come back in an hr, get seated outside even though there are plenty of spaces inside. Fine. Drink wifey ordered was the best part of the experience.

Can we order the cauliflower - no, we are out of our most popular item. Ok.

Guac appetizer - made from half an avocado and a thousand chips. $12 

Salad with ahi - 1 dimensional salad with 3 pieces of ahi. Ahi was good wish there was more of it. Salad had no diversity anything interesting $23

Chicken kabobs - supposed to be with ginger terriyaki and sesame and garlic. Only thing I could taste
was terriyaki, very heavy handed.
 
Nothing we ordered was beyond marginal...

name: Customer_7713
comments: Service and food was excellent!! Personal favorite is the beef short rib tacos washed down with a gluten-free beer.

name: Customer_1272
comments: Got the turkey blt. Excellent! Service was a little slow but we weren't in a rush.

name: Customer_7541
comments: One of my favorite spots in town. Burger is amazing, good vibe, nice staff. Go-to gastro pub for sure.

name: Customer_6303
comments: Gastropub delight! I have to stop here every time I come to Nashville for business. I haven't had a single thing from the menu that I did not love. The grilled cheese was amazing, the soup tasty, the drinks... Mmmmmmm. Try the one with agave. The truffle fries are perfect, and be sure to top it all off with s'mores you make at the table. I've enjoyed eating outside, inside, at the bar... and have taken food to go when I didn't have time to relax. The decor is rustic and interesting. Depending on the time of day, it can be a quiet spot to relax or it can get really noisy at happy hour. The one drawback is the prices. A bit on the high side, but okay for someone like me who only does this occasionally for a treat. If you were a local, it might set you back if you became a regular.

name: Customer_1368
comments: Had brunch here yesterday with my son and his new wife (as of Saturday), and I couldn't have been more impressed! We had a party of 10 and were seated fairly quickly in a nice area with a tv. The two for one drinks were deliciuos and the eggs Benedict were hands down the best I've ever had! The service was absolutely outstanding! We had Nikki as our server not only was she friendly, helpful, and entertaining- she also took the time to comp the drinks for the newlyweds. I will definetly come back to Tavern. One of the best brunches in Nashville! I will be recommending it as much as I can, and if you go- ask for Nikki, best service I've had at a restaurant!

name: Customer_1353
comments: A group of 13, including myself, showed up for a late dinner on Saturday night and while we did expect a wait, we did not expect a 1.5-2 hr wait, considering there were two empty tables inside waiting to be cleared. It was not crowded I should add. The drinks were also a little overpriced, especially since that was pretty much the only option you had for a 2 hour wait. The staff would not allow one under 21 person in our group to stay and even be served just for dinner, so naturally we were all forced to leave AFTER we had already ordered a drink. Despite the staff being professional, we felt it was rude to force our entire party to leave since we had already committed to waiting the 1.5-2 hrs that was expected. We took our business across the street. While the food may be amazing here, I suggest not coming with a party of 2 or more unless you want to be tired, hangry, and spend at least $20 on drinks alone prior to even reading a dinner menu.

name: Customer_5176
comments:
3 stars for food and a 1/2 star for ambience/drink specials. Went here with a bunch of friends on a Wednesday night. The place was busy! They said our wait was about 30 min so we decided to go to the bar. 2 for 1 drink special!! Excellent! The drinks were pretty big and strong so it was a great deal. I got the tequila drink with blackberry and agave juice (can't remember the name). It was good!! We sat on the outdoor patio with our drinks while we waited for our name...it was perfect! 

The food was mehhh...I had the lamb tacos which were just ok. I felt like they needed to be more exciting...there was barely anything on them. I ordered 3 because I was pretty hungry, and it was the perfect size. My friend who got the burger loved it, so maybe I just had to order something else. Who knows. Overall I was underwhelmed. I have to eat gluten free (Celiac), and they did have a gluten free menu. It wasn't huge but enough options. However, they did have fried things on the gf menu that are NOT GF!! This is a huge pet peeve of mine...why put it on the gluten free menu if it's not?! So annoying. I would go back to this place for drinks only.

name: Customer_9258
comments: You'll definitely have a wait for brunch but grab a drink and buckle in cause it's worth it. Everyone at the table loved what they ordered. We started with the buffalo cauliflower and got the pretzel pancakes, nooner, blueberry waffle and the red velvet waffle and damn if we didn't clean our plates. Also if you don't get the white trash hash you'll regret it for years to come. Service was great and our drinks were perfect.

name: Customer_9503
comments: Delicious food in a fun setting.  Great helpful and friendly service.  Two levels of seating near the bar.  We had awesome buffalo cauliflower, egg rolls with philly cheese steak and amazing kale salad.  highly recommend the Tavern.

name: Customer_9433
comments: PSA: Just go for the 2 for 1 drink special at brunch and white trash hash. The atmosphere is trendy. Everything else is not worth the wait! We arrived at 11am on a Friday for brunch, was told the wait was 20 mins. We did not get seated until 11:50a. Food is average. I will say the nachos were good but nothing outstanding. The biscuits came out cold. A "side" of bacon is $5 dollars and you get seriously 2 slices. Service was very very slow. Wouldn't recommend unless you have 3.5 hours or more to kill for brunch.

name: Customer_1514
comments:
Tavern was in walking distance from our hotel, and we had read it was a good place to watch a game, so we were there! I really liked the feel of this place. It was really modern and even the waitstaff complements the look with their matching grey v-necks. We were famished after a long day and got down on so many dishes! 

-grilled artichokes. promised with a "comeback sauce" which we got to help my friend push ahead past her hangover, it didn't really do that.
-lamb tacos and pork tacos. the lamb tacos were great but nothing could compare to the pork tacos. I have never been more sad to see the end of a taco.
-salad of little gems. hello? little gems describing anything? I'm in! It was a great, little refreshment from my all-meat diet, with cranberries and fresh mozzerella.
-chicken and waffle. The fried chicken was great, but the cheddar and jalepeno waffle was almost too overpowering with the sweey syrup.
-loco moco. too much meat but the rice and egg were just what my friend needed to get back on the drinking horse so props for that!

The drink list was also amazing here, great whiskey cocktails and they make a mean martini as well! I also liked the mix of people here. It was the perfect Friday night crowd. Prices were pretty reasonable, unless, of course, you are posted up watching Michigan beat Kansas in overtime, then the bill might be a bit higher to taste victory ;)

name: Customer_3935
comments: I had high hopes after hearing good things and reading good reviews from numerous sites. A friend and I went for brunch and while we waited 45 minutes for a table, that was expected. After being seated our waitress took our drink orders and came back about 5 minutes later with waters and another 10 with my friend's blood orange mimosa. We ordered and waited over an hour for our food. When the waitress finally checked on us I asked about the toast for my son because I knew he was hungry. She came back 10 minutes later with our meal which, to my dismay, was disappointing. I've had better food at a local diner in town and for half the price. I have no idea how long our food sat under heat lamps but my white trash hash was cold and the eggs on the nooner I ordered were overcooked. My friend ordered the roasted peppers and squashes and said hers was good but she couldn't eat the hash. The service was pretty crummy. We had to ask for our check and then we had to ask the hostess for someone to check us out because our waitress must have forgotten about us. Overall it was a dismal experince and while I was excited to take my husband the next time we are in Nashville, I think we'll be eating elsewhere.

name: Customer_1008
comments: Came in for lunch while in Nashville in business. The waitress sold me on their Bloody Mary, so I ordered that and the lettuce wraps. The bloody was ridiculously watered down. It tasted watered down and looked like the glass was about 85% water/ice. When I commented on the look and taste, the waitress proceeded to tell me that if it looked watered down, there was probably extra vodka in it, which I couldn't taste because it was "infused" which cuts down on the vodka taste. What a load of BS. It was one of the most disappointing bloodies I've had. I should have sent it back, but she was adamant that I was wrong. Lettuce wraps had a nice spicy kick, which I liked, but it failed to redeem the dry, canned-tasting chicken. Very. Under-impressed.

name: Customer_5291
comments:
First night in Nashville, after a long car ride, ready to get a taste of that night life!!  Great place to start.

Food: Started with the SHISHITO PEPPERS, def glad I did.  These are perfectly charred.  Cooked well, so that they are still a little crisp and not soggy.  Lightly salted.  Greatest part, they give a little pile of sea salt on the side, so you can season to your liking!!  Be careful with these.  Some of the peppers have a super spicy kick.
  
BUFFALO CAULIFLOWER was another starter.  This app was a bit too sour for me.  The tanginess was pretty potent that I could not focus on any other flavors.  Also, the exterior of the cauliflower was not that crispy.  More on the soggier side.  Not a fan.  Pass on this.
  
TURKEY BLT was a good choice.  The pretzel bread was nice and chewy.  Lovely choice of bread for this sammy.  Wonderfully smoked turkey with crispy bacon.  Comes together beautifully with the smooth gruyere cheese, and the creamy avocado aioli.  Great textures and tastes that really comes together in this sammy.  I got it with the Tuscan tavern fries.  Nice and crunchy fries.  Def try.

SMORES on the tabletop.  Even comes with a small campfire.  Classic fix'ns for smores: graham crackers, marshmellows, and chocolate bar.  In addition, some strawberries and reese's peanut butter cups.  Was quite the indoor smores experience.

Service: Drinks were full, food got to the table fresh and hot, server was attentive, and table was cleared away promptly.  All together, I think it was a good experience.

Ambiance: Very casual.  Rustic and slightly romantic.  Nice for a girls gathering, as well as date night. 
  
Dranks: Great selection of beers, wines, and specialty cocktails.  A little something for everyone.  I had wine that night, but def would like to go back and try one of their cocktails.  
 
Overall: A place that I would like to visit again.  Food was good.  Drinks were good.  This is a place that you can go, no pressure, find something to eat, and get your drink on.  Enjoy!!

name: Customer_1238
comments: A friend recommended this restaurant to me while on a business trip to Nashville. The food and service were great! It's a really cool atmosphere with lots of fresh air. Unique menu items, and everything that I saw come out looked so good.

comments:
my favorite brunch spot on nashville! 

the drinks are amazing and they have a wide range of items on the menu. my favorite brunch items are probably the benedicts and white trash hash.

my favorite items served all day are the sweet potato fries and tuscan kale salad!

the only complaint I would have is that they usually have a long wait, especially for brunch so come early and be prepared to wait! it's certainly worth it. 

other than that, the atmosphere and food are some
of the best in nashville!

name: Customer_4138
comments:
Not my cuppa gin. Probably because of all that basil.

Tavern is big, a bit brash, bro-friendly with all the TVs and reasonably priced for its prime location on Broadway. Drop your name and cell phone number at the host stand and get sexted when your table is ready. So tech.

Reviews sing praises of their prime beef burgers, so wifey and I opted for a pair, each with bacon and cheese. Subbing a side salad for fries comes with a surcharge... the amount will totally surprise you. (Clickbait header fail: It's $3.50.)

With the fixin's and the greens, a $9.50 patty sizzled up to $16. And the lasting impression is nil, save the need for seasoning and a Maillard crust. It's an average burger that should be $8 at any pub, which gives me pause as to why it comes so highly praised. An off-night in the kitchen? Labor Day weekend lethargy? Unclear. The end result just didn't resonate.

Could cocktails save the day? Her berry julep was all pulp and my 1920 (a gin, grapefruit, ginger and basil concoction borrowed from Brinkley's) tasted only of the green leaf. No tartness, no ginger bite, no other herbal subtleties from the spirit. Just basil. All the basil. At least they were cheap-ish!

name: Customer_8861
comments: Chose Tavern because I wanted to catch a baseball game on their TVs while eating. The wait for a table of four was an hour on a Saturday night. Food was fine but nothing to jump up and down about. Waitress recommended the Tavern burger...it was ok.

comments: Decided to try this place after our Airbnb host recommended it. Total miss! Way too overpriced for what we got. We ordered guacamole because they were out of cauliflower. The guacamole was too plain, lacking salt and spice. The size was ridiculously small and disproportional to the amount of chips you get with it. We also had chicken skewers, that were described as "sesame, garlic, ginger...". It literally tasted like chicken with some super sweet teriyaki sauce. The rice with it was totally plain too. We had kale salad with ahi tuna. Also was lacking taste, and the size of kale and tuna was disproportional. Not worth the money at all.

name: Customer_1708
comments: SUPER DISAPPOINTED...recommended by a friend, came here to have a drink and an appetizer with my boyfriend, sat down at 5 o'clock at the bar and waited 25 minutes before we decided to get up and walk out. The bar was hardly full, 2 seats available as soon as we walked in and the restaurant itself was relatively empty. The bartender walked down and helped another couple but never acknowledged us. Hope others have a better experience because it is a good looking restaurant.

name: Customer_5831
comments:
Tavern is probably one of the better brunch places in Nashville IF (and only if) you go with friends. This is not the place to go for a brunch date or to go with any person that you actually want to have a conversation with.

Both times that my wife and I have gone (once by ourselves, and the other time with some friends) the music has been extremely loud - like to the point where we have been yelling just to hear each other. Not kidding. Look, I like my music loud... and their playlist was actually on point (late 90's/early 2000's hits)... but going out to eat is a social experience. Part of sharing a meal is enjoying the company of the people you're with. Don't blast music in my face and force me to lean in just to hear what the person next to me is saying. C'mon. 

On to the food! It's GREAT. I highly recommend the Benedict Uno - a short rib benedict topped with tabasco-infused hollandaise. Wow. So much amazing flavor in every bite. I savored it right down to the end. I also recommend the maple fondue if you're with a group. It's a fun dish to share and has assorted fruits and some french toast and sausage... all to be dipped in a delicious warm maple syrup mixture. Can't go wrong. Also, don't sleep on the 2-for-1 libations. The blood orange mimosa and the red sangria are my favorites (although the last time I went, I just doubled up on the sangria... easily my favorite).

This place deserves respect for the quality of food they put out and their decent pricing (average about $12-$15 per entree). The only things that keep this from being a 4-star review are the noise level, the lack of parking (bring cash because you will need to use the valet), and the fact that you will undoubtedly have a wait. When we went with our friends, we got their 10 minutes after they opened and were told there was a 20-30 minute wait. We ended up actually waiting almost an hour. Not really a complaint, since you have to factor in a wait at popular places... but still. Just a warning - you will have a wait.

Give this place a shot if you like good food for brunch, just go in knowing that there are some pitfalls with this place.

name: Customer_5973
comments:
Was in Nashville this past weekend with some friends. Decided to try this place as it was close to where we were staying. 

The place is very quaint on the inside. Dark lighting, the type of spot that could suffice a first date, a work event or a family get together. My friend and I showed up around 3pm and strangely there was a ten minute wait (Which is weird, because it's that awkward time in between lunch and dinner, but whatever.) 

Our server is super friendly and attentive. I order the pan seared tuna with a side of the sweet potato fries with jalapeno ketchup. My friend orders the tavern burger. 

Our food comes. I take a bite of my tuna and it appears raw, almost entirely uncooked. I try again and can't bare it. The waiter has no problem swapping my order for the salmon which is very kind of him. My friend appears to enjoy the burger. The fries are fine-- not seven dollar side worthy fine, but decent enough. The jalapeno ketchup tastes like regular ketchup. The salmon doesn't particularly taste like fish (almost like an overly marinated chicken, which wouldn't be a bad thing if it wasn't brought under the guise of fish) but I run through it because I'm starved. We pay and the meal for me was at its best below average. Especially for the cost. 

Naturally the evening/early morning hits and I've got all types of food poisoning and stomach bug type issues (diarrhea, nauseous, headache, puking.) This was Monday morning/ Sunday evening. It's now Thursday and I'm still ill. Not quite sure how these people are cleaning their meats, but I won't be back anytime soon. Nice, attentive staff and sweet vibe. Food was awful.

name: Customer_6345
comments: Food was great.  Sweet potato chips were amazing.  Great vibe too.  Seating indoors or out and a huge variety of menu options.

name: Customer_2340
comments: Tavern has a nice variety of healthy options. They have a large section titled "yolks" which consists of the many different and funky ways you can serve an egg (we had one with salmon in an omelette and it was delicious). We also had the "trail mix" which consisted of bulgur, quinoa, and other healthy perks... a great way to start the morning. 2/1 brunch libations - I would recommend the Cucumber Mary.

name: Customer_1923
comments: tavern is above average and the american food is pretty good here. I like the ambiance and the TV in the restaurant. The drinks are good as well. It's in a neat area that is right next to bars and the division places

name: Customer_2113
comments:
This may seem like a standard American burger joint, but they actually have taken pains to create a thoughtful and surprising menu. 

There are options ranging from middle eastern to Mediterranean to Indian to new American and I had a sampling of them all. Everything had a distinct flavor profile, regardless of whether I liked it, and the burger was one of the best I've had in Nashville. Oh, and for dessert you can roast your own marshmallows at the table. 

Service wasn't the greatest, but not terrible as other reviews have noted and overall this is a spot I'd recommend.

name: Customer_5435
comments: Great brunch and cocktails! The Nooner, Roasted Peppers and Squash, and Blueberry Waffles were great. Very good Bloody Mary, red sangria, and signature craft cocktails.

name: Customer_6263
comments: Fantastic brunch, bloody Mary's and blood orange mimosas were superb. The Red Velvet waffles, cheddar cheese, chorizo and gravy biscuits were great too and you must try the huevos rancheros, they will not disappoint. The service was also great.

name: Customer_3292
comments: Nice bar with good music and lively atmosphere. The beef Tacos were so Yummy, and so were the fries. Went if there happy

name: Customer_9015
comments: The pork chops were delicious. Yummy burger. Good beer and cocktail selection, nice decor. It was busy when we were there, so a little loud.

name: Customer_9668
comments: PSA: Just go for the 2 for 1 drink special at brunch and white trash hash.  The atmosphere is trendy. Everything else is not worth the wait! We arrived at 11am on a Friday for brunch, was told the wait was 20 mins. We did not get seated until 11:50a. Food is average. I will say the nachos were good but nothing outstanding. The biscuits came out cold. A "side" of bacon is $5 dollars and you get seriously 2 slices. Service was very very slow. Wouldn't recommend unless you have 3.5 hours or more  to kill for brunch.

name: Customer_8726
comments: Place was awesome! Went here for my birthday & I had a large party of 12, they included gratuity with the bill. But the waitress was very nice! Good music & environment. I will definetly be coming to this place again!!!

name: Customer_9754
comments: Another Yelper hit it -- this is a noisy, crowded restaurant with big screen TVs. I wouldn't call it a sports bar. Nothing wrong with the place. Cool location, good beer selection. The food - deliciuos, but eliminates itself as a "sports bar". My sons and I wanted to catch some pub grub and the hockey game. Got the game. The grub-- eclectic. Do go here if you want a busy, bustling, energetic, tasty, flavorful, thumping music-beat experince. Don't go here if you want a burger, a beer and a hockey game amidst sports conversation.

name: Customer_2124
comments: I am now obsessed with Tavern. I'm from out of town and was just in for the weekend, but it was the best meal I have had in awhile (the smoked salmon Benedict w the hash). The hash was unreal! Everyone loved their meals, as well as the great drink specials (buy one get one). The sangria was great on a Saturday morning patio and our server Melissa was so so sweet! Amazing service plus an amazing personality and delicious food. I wish I lived in Nashville so I could eat here weekly. Enjoy it! Cheers!

name: Customer_4216
comments: I was so disappointed that my 2nd Tavern experince wasn't as flawless as my first one. I'm only giving it 3 stars due to the service we received from the manager and because most of the food was still good. I met 3 friends for a late Saturday brunch, 2 of which had never been there before. I was excited to introduce them to Tavern's fabulousness but left feeling a little embarrassed after the service we received. For starters, it took about 20 minutes before our server even acknowledged us. I asked about drink specials and as soon as the last word came out of her mouth she walked away leaving me unable to order a drink. About 10 minutes later she finally came back. After ordering drinks it took another 10 minutes to get them. We were ready to order our meals (had been for about 30 minutes) but again, she walked away before we could do so. Instead, she sauntered on over to the bar and proceeded to talk and flirt with some guy at the bar for over 20 minutes. We timed it. At that point we were so disgusted that we stopped another server walking by and asked if we could order with her. She was happy to help us. My 3 friends ordered the Tavern burger and they all liked it. I opted for a ham and brie omelette and it was kind of meh. I remembered I don't like brie (my fault for ordering it) and I had to pick it all out. The omelette was lacking flavor anyway. I should have at least salt and peppered it myself, I guess. The side of white trash hash was very tasty but an extremely small serving. Only about 5 bites. Because of our shitty server we were never offered to order a second round of drinks and it was past happy hour since of course we had been sitting at the table for almost 2 hours at that point. Dirty dishes sat on our table for 30 minutes while we waited for our checks. During our 2 hours at the table our server only came around 3 times. Very disappointing. With the exception of the burgers my friends had, the dining experience was pretty terrible. We ended up speaking with Madeline, the manager, about our experiance. She was very nice and seemed to sincerely care about what we had to say. She ended up comping our entire meal and gave us some coupons to come back and try brunch again. However, while we were speaking with Madeline the server in question was whispering and giggling with a busboy and staring at our table. Our point of "complaining" was truly not to get anything free, but to let these little brats know that people aren't just going to stand by and let them slack on their job while they run around and socialize. We ended up tipping the server who actually took our order. I'm hoping this horrible expereince was just a fluke because I really like Tavern and want to continue coming back.

name: Customer_6135
comments: I literally had the best grilled salmon of my life here! This place is amazing. The food is extremely good. My husband had chimichanga and he is also very happy  with his food. The service was great too. I can't recommend this place more!

name: Customer_6364
comments: Good fun place, appetizers are fun, and different! Place is always full of nice people, good energy. Great for large or small groups. Fun times!

name: Customer_2759
comments:
If you think you are walking into a typical bar menu .... think again!  Wonderful, original recipes.  I had a kale salad, guacamole and chicken wings.  All awesome with non conventional ingredients (finally chopped kale with parmesan cheese, nuts, lemon).  Guacamole with pistachio nuts and goat cheese!  Who would have thought!!

Really good!

name: Customer_9135
comments: Decided to try this place after our Airbnb host recommended it. Total miss! Way too overpriced for what we got. We ordered guacamole because they were out of cauliflower. The guacamole was too plain, lacking salt and spice. The size was ridiculously small and disproportional to the amount of chips you get with it. We also had chicken skewers, that were described as "sesame, garlic, ginger...". It literally tasted like chicken with some super sweet teriyaki sauce. The rice with it was totally plain too. We had kale salad with ahi tuna. Also was lacking taste, and the size of kale and tuna was disproportional. Not worth the money at all.

name: Customer_5209
comments: Jalepeno margaritas. Grilled artichokes. Mac and cheese. Amazing.

name: Customer_6576
comments: Horrible service! Restaurant was recommended so we decided to check it out. First time in Nashville so we wanted to see what the downtown experince was, and we were greatly disappointed; mostly due to our unfortunate experiance at tavern. We waited for 20 minutes without any acknowledgement from our waiter. When we finally saw him in our area he greeted a table who had just arrived, skipped our table and went on to another. We ended up leaving the establishment. I repeat...horrible service!!!! I guess I can take that back, it wasn't horrible, there WAS NO SERVICE!

name: Customer_9465
comments: Food is great, drinks are great, deals are great (Brunch with 2-4-1 drinks? Heck yeah!). The menu is extensive and interesting, with unique twists on classic dishes. The srvice is also great, but I am withholding a fifth star due to the management's seating policies. We came for brunch on a Sunday expecting an hour plus wait, so when the hostess informed us it would be 1hr45m we weren't surprised. However, we became frustrated when we noticed there were 4 open tables on the patio that still hadn't been seated after an hour of waiting. It was a beautiful day so we asked the hostess about it and she said that the tables were reserved. When we asked again, she explained that the patio tables were not assigned to a specific server but were instead added on to a server's load inside, so they weren't seating them because they didn't want to overwhelm the servers. Totally understandable to not want to overwork your servers, but why not seat people with the caveat that servic will be slower? Or better yet, why not specifically assign a server to the outdoor section so that wait times will be lower? Having worked in the service industry, our group was confused by this. We ended up just sitting at one of the empty patio tables until the hostess notified us that a table was ready. We ordered the Cheddar Biscuit, the Wood Fire Double Yokes, and a Turkey Feta Omelette from the specials board and all were delicious. The biscuit comes in a trio and though it doesn't look like a lot of food they are VERY filling. Our server surprised us with a side of White Trash Hash on the house because our food was taking longer than expected (we didn't even notice the timing, so it was a very nice gesture). The White Trash Hash is a must, this stuff is addicting! Potatoes, rice, and gooey cheese- who could ask for more. Overall, great place for brunch in Nashville. Expect a long line but food worth the wait. Hopefully management can improve their seating policies to cut down on wait times in the future.

name: Customer_7077
comments:
Not my cuppa gin. Probably because of all that basil.

Tavern is big, a bit brash, bro-friendly with all the TVs and reasonably priced for its prime location on Broadway. Drop your name and cell phone number at the host stand and get sexted when your table is ready. So tech.

Reviews sing praises of their prime beef burgers, so wifey and I opted for a pair, each with bacon and cheese. Subbing a side salad for fries comes with a surcharge... the amount will totally surprise you. (Clickbait header fail: It's $3.50.)

With the fixin's and the greens, a $9.50 patty sizzled up to $16. And the lasting impression is nil, save the need for seasoning and a Maillard crust. It's an average burger that should be $8 at any pub, which gives me pause as to why it comes so highly praised. An off-night in the kitchen? Labor Day weekend lethargy? Unclear. The end result just didn't resonate.

Could cocktails save the day? Her berry julep was all pulp and my 1920 (a gin, grapefruit, ginger and basil concoction borrowed from Brinkley's) tasted only of the green leaf. No tartness, no ginger bite, no other herbal subtleties from the spirit. Just basil. All the basil. At least they were cheap-ish!

name: Customer_8581
comments: Good fun place, appetizers are fun, and different! Place is always full of nice people, good energy. Great for large or small groups. Fun times!

name: Customer_8403
comments: A group of 13, including myself, showed up for a late dinner on Saturday night and while we did expect a wait, we did not expect a 1.5-2 hr wait, considering there were two empty tables inside waiting to be cleared. name: Customer_8117
comments: I'm usually a chilaquiles girl, so the Huevos Rancheros sounded sort of tempting with its eggs, tortillas and salsa combination. Now, huevos rancheros in general has never really appealed to me, but Tavern had me changing my tune. I have a feeling that no other restaurant's version of this dish will impress me as much as this one, but if you are in Nashville and you are at Tavern for brunch and you don't get the Huevos Rancheros.... you're making a HUGE mistake. One of the best brunch meals of my life y'all...

name: Customer_9827
comments: We came here because of all the great yelp reviews, I can't believe this is 4-stars.. Good beer selection, good atmosphere, and decent service.  The food, however, was bla.. We really wanted to try the fried chicken skins, they came out very hard and very stuck together.  The sauce had good flavor but the skins came in a clump that we could hardly break apart. Our food came out about 4 minutes I into our attempt to chisel the skins apart. Kaya toast was weird and really lacked anything to bring the dish together.  After scraping off the sauce it was basically Texas toast and an egg.  The 2 sets of tacos we ordered were both overcooked and VERY dry. Come here for drinks, skip the food!

name: Customer_7929
comments:
I have seen various reviews on Tavern.  Some very negative.  Others slightly positive.  Most complimented the food but nothing spectacular. 

So, this past Friday night a few friends and I got together for dinner and I wanted to try some place new.  I put out a list of 3 new places (new to me anyway) I'd like to try - based upon the Menu.  I listed Red Pony in Franklin, Burger Up and Tavern.  I sent my friends links to the restaurants and ultimately we agreed that Tavern would be the place.  

We arrived at 7:30 and ended up having to wait an hour for a table and they don't take reservations.  That was fine.  We figured about anywhere we went on a Friday night at this point we would encounter a wait of similar length.  So, we waited and ordered a couple cocktails while we waited.  

This is probably the biggest downside of the restaurant.  They don't have a place for you to really wait.  The bar was jam packed and there was no seating up front.  There was seating outside on the patio - but no one was out there because it was raining and cold.  So, we stood inside near the door for an hour.  

When we were finally seated the server asked us if we needed any more drinks and if we wanted any appetizers.

We decided to go with the 'Bazooka" Guacamole Appetizer.  I pretty much hate Guacamole and never order it anywhere.  I've tried it several times many different places.  Never liked it.  But, this was supposed to be 'different' with some goat cheese and other stuff in it as well.  The presentation of the appetizer was very cool.  They bring it out in a 2-3" deep round cake pan lined with parchment or wax paper - I don't really remember.  Inside there is a glass jar with one of those hinged glass lids on top and its filled with this guacamole concoction.  They have a few chips out on the pan, however, there is also a small, brown paper bag with the logo of 'Tavern' on it - and it is filled with chips.  We took the small server spoon and each took a dollop of the guacamole and put it on a chip.  Wow!  Absolutely incredible.  I don't know if it qualifies as guacamole or not (I'm sure some purists would say it doesn't) - but whatever it is or whatever you want to call it - it was incredible.  I couldn't get enough.  We were scraping the bottom of the jar trying to get every last ounce of this wonderful, tasty spread.

Moving onto dinner two of us go the Tavern Burger.  This burger is made with Prime Rib and Filet.  2 excellent cuts of meat - ground up and made into a burger.  I had mine with White Cheddar and bacon and was incredible!  Everything was good.  The meat, the bacon, the cheese - even the bun was tasty.  My friend had his plain and loved it as well.  Both burgers were served with fries.  He had the regular fries - I had mine tossed in Parmesan and garlic.  Either way they were good.  Apparently they serve them several different ways.

Another friend got the 'Mama Sans Fried Chicken'.  He was blown away by how much food he got.  He also was surprised at how well the chicken went with the cold noodles he was served as the side.  He said the cold noodles were a good juxtaposition against the hot chicken. 

My other friend got the "Salad of Little Gems".  It looked a bit small to me but he claimed to really enjoy it.  As far as salads go it did look great.

The food was all served rather quickly but the pacing of the meal was on point.  The appetizer was served and finished well ahead of the meal making its way from the kitchen.  Too often I feel rushed and sometimes the appetizers and entree arrive within second of each other.  Sometimes even together!  I think the pacing of the meal was excellent.  Also, our server was great and our glasses were never empty.  She made sure we always had plenty to drink.

4 Cocktails, 4 entree's, 1 appetizer = $94 bucks after tax and everything.  So, around 20 bucks a person for a night out.  

So, to review:

Long wait - no place to really sit.  They DO take your phone number and will call you when your table is ready so you can make your way back to the restaurant.

Service was excellent.  Drinks were never empty.  Pacing of meal was great from the appetizer to the main course.

Price was fine.  We could have eaten for less if we didn't get cocktails, appetizers AND the main course.  If we'd just had water and our meal - we would have spent a lot less.  The cocktails were pricy - but pretty stout.  They didn't skimp on the alcohol for sure.

I think it was wonderful and we are already planning our next trip!  I think you should too.

name: Customer_9267
comments:
Oh, Brunch at Tavern. I'm so sad that it took me so long to visit you. 

I'll keep this brief: The dishes here are superbly crafted. Flavors are lovely and multifaceted, and the plating is gorgeous. My favorite dishes, though, are easy to pinpoint. 

First up is the Sweet Potato Chips, which arrive at your table with a curry salt and blue cheese fondue. This is a perfect start to any meal, and honestly, I could probably be happy just munching on these while sipping a few cocktails (which I'll get to in a moment). As for a main course, though: The Benedict Dos. Poached eggs, smoked salmon, and a creamy hollandaise? Delicious doesn't even begin to cover it. 

I will admit that I find myself rather addicted to their Blood Orange Mimosa, so I haven't actually tried anything else on the menu. However, one of my closest friends loved the Bloody Mary, and their beer selection is impressive and was mat with easy approval from our group a few weeks ago. 

Is it loud? Yes. 
Is it expensive? Sure, although most of the cocktails are two for one. 
But is it worth the insanely long wait? Absolutely.

name: Customer_9726
comments:
We totally blew off all Nashville brunch recommendations just because the menu at Tavern looked so good.  Risky move, bucking the suggestions of former residents and frequent visitors, but I'm happy to report it paid off handsomely.  

I looove the set-up of the restaurant.  There's a covered/open air area, a bar area with some booths and high-top tables, then a cozy area "upstairs" overlooking the action so to speak.  It basically has a seating location for whatever your mood.  Very cool.

The brunch menu was almost impossible to choose from.  Our eyes went directly to the red velvet waffle with cream cheese drizzle.  We're not big sweets for breakfast folks but we do love our desserts.  But the inevitable was sure to occur, eat brunch and be too full - rule of thumb - order your sweets at the same time as your meal if you're determined to try something.  So we did....

I opted for the benedict uno which was fantastic.  Tender braised short ribs on an english muffin with perfectly cooked poached eggs and a Tabasco hollandaise.  Soooo incredibly good and the hollandaise was the perfect combination of buttery and spicy.  Excellent.  I will say, if you don't love hollandaise you would be put off - my plate was literally swimming in sauce (arm floaties and all...)  I gobbled it up but it turned my wife off from trying it (note to self, don't bath in hollandaise.)

My wife opted for the The Nooner which is an omelet with bacon, fried oysters and a
spicy sour cream, served with "white trash hash" (basically a heavily hashbrown casserole.)   So back to the red velvet wafftle....we didn't finish it....I know...I know....we tried and we did a pretty good job, but we just couldn't.  It was super good although almost not quite done in the middle, but tasty nonetheless.  

Good service, good food, great atmosphere (would love to watch a game here and snack my way through the day.)  Can't wait to return!

name: Customer_6727
comments: I have never been so insulted and talked down to in my life. Michelle, I think that's her name it's on my receipt but she never introduced herself, was the rudest person I have ever given my money to in my life. When we sat down she was talking about personal issues with the barback loud enough for us to hear and I thought that was odd in and off itself. When she gave us our menus she said a few times "these menus are good for the next 30 seconds."  Sorry but either give us brunch or give us dinner menus and explain that the kitchen is in the midst of a shift change, don't make us feel pressured because you dropped menus that have an extremely short time limit. Instead of eating we decided to just get drinks. She let us know that the brunch menu libations were, her words, 2 for 1. We ordered a mimosa off the list and hung out. When we got get drinks they set two wooden tokens down but didn't reference the at all, so we didn't know what they were for.  Eventually ordered some food off the dinner menu to go. She was very non existent the whole time we were sitting at the bar, not attentive at all. When we asked for the bill I saw that both our drinks were on there. I asked about them and let her know about the 2 for 1 statement she said. She then proceeded to tell me it was buy one, get one and that's what the tokens are for. I told her that "buy one get one" and "2 for 1" are different and if we knew it was BOGO we would have ordered another drink (if she would have even paid attention to us).  After a little back and forth she said she would take care of it and that "they weren't trying to screw us."  She talked to us like we were the worst people on earth because she doesn't know how to explain her own restaurants policies. I work in an industry that has me visiting 10-15 bars/restaurants/hotels a day and I have never had a worse hospitality experience in my life. Tavern Management - this employee is losing you revenue left and right.  Not only is she not taking care of customers and grabbing reorders, she is turning people away for good. This treatment was so horrible and off putting that I am going to go out of my way to recommended against going to Tavern due to the disrespect we felt. Hopefully your floor managers recognize how bad she is and theyo do something about it because she is taking money out of your pocket every shift she works.

name: Customer_6375
comments:
I've never been to an M Street restaurant before, for those of you who are not familiar with M Street they are the zany people who bring us restaurant concepts such as Kayne Prime (on my bucket list,) Virago and Moto (also on my bucket list.) So on Wednesday night we visited Tavern, which is self-described as "a pub for chefs."

Valet parking at this location is a must and they were prompt and efficient. There was plenty of porch seating available as well as being used - Nashvillians do love their porches. The inside of the restaurant had a rustic feel and it seemed as though the bar top was inhabited by business class regulars. That having been said I could easily picture the bar at 12 midnight being inhabited by waitrons and people with checkered pants, it would be a great place to have some concept drinks and small plates after a busy restaurant shift.

I ordered the Korean short rib tacos - I definitely got the red pepper forward taste as well as the cool of the cucumber and cilantro. I would order it again. Delivery time was about 13 minutes, a good ticket time.

It's very evident that these people are "on their game," I will be returning to try other items on their menu. And one day I will visit Kayne Prime, I might splurge for that on my father's birthday. Visit Tavern, have fun!

name: Customer_3222
comments: Just stopped in for drinks.  Staff was great,  never felt rushed. Food passing by smelt and looked awesome. May be coming back tomorrow.

name: Customer_9698
comments: Just walked into the Tavern Nashville and was served by the brightest smile in the world. Thank you Heather , amazing server.

name: Customer_6470
comments: My family ate here last night and thought the food and srvice were excelent.

name: Customer_8378
comments:
Great staff, service and food!

I ordered the kale salad (OMGosh - good!), short ribs tacos and the fried cauliflower- a MUST - even if you don't finish it all.

name: Customer_2659
comments: Food and service was great! Try the BLT and the egg rolls! The drinks are so good as well.

name: Customer_4931
comments: Burger was great. Cooked perfectly, but nothing special. Packed for brunch specials. Seem to have awesome election of cocktails and awesome bartenders. Was there for food, don't really drink. Def would go back. Atmosphere was great too.

name: Customer_5833
comments: Ordered to go through Uber Eats. Great burger and fries. A little pricey but the to go containers made it worth it. 4 stars only bc it was a little cold by time it got to my house. Will order again soon.

name: Customer_7753
comments:
Had brunch here yesterday with my son and his new wife (as of Saturday), and I couldn't have been more impressed! We had a party of 10 and were seated fairly quickly in a nice area with a tv. 
The two for one drinks were delicious and the eggs Benedict were hands down the best I've ever had! 
The service was absolutely outstanding! We had Nikki as our server not only was she friendly, helpful, and entertaining- she also took the time to comp the drinks for the newlyweds. 
I will definitely come back to Tavern. One of the best brunches in Nashville! I will be recommending it as much as I can, and if you go- ask for Nikki, best service I've had at a restaurant!
