name: Customer_7020
comments: Terrible wait (unnecessary), average service, above average prices, and excruciating wait for food. Find someplace else. There's lots to choose from.

name: Customer_9076
comments: The environment is great!  It's a multi-level facility that puts a modern spin on the old "tavern" concept.  I was impressed with the food I ordered as well as the cocktails.  The waitstaff was quite personable and made the experience even more enjoyable.  My only critique was the homemade ice cream I tried for dessert.  It simply wasn't good. Of course, nobody's perfect.  I would definitely go back to Tavern again.  :-)

name: Customer_9994
comments: Nice little cozy spot. Atmosphere is casual and classy. I had the chicken skewers with rice. It was very tasty and light. Also had a margarita that was fantastic! I only like fresh margaritas and this one passed the test. Recommend checking it out.

name: Customer_9102
comments: Great vegetarian options (I got the Buffalo cauliflower - amazing), healthy options (chopped kale salad with almonds and dried blueberries with light dressing), as well as favorites like tacos, nachos, fried chicken and burgers.  Lots of tvs but also more secluded tables. Would definitely come back!

name: Customer_9593
comments: Seriously, the best place I've been to in Nashville (so far). The food was excellent, and there is plenty of variety to make everyone happy. Definitely eating here again soon.

name: Customer_7693
comments:
Food tastes good but not worth the price. Drinks are overpriced as well. $11.50 for a small Moscow mule with stolii vodka. 

I got the grilled cheese and the grilled chicken skewers. Both tasted fine but nothing to write home about. The chicken came with rice but everything was very plain, nothing that would warrant the price I paid. My tab totaled $61 after tip for grilled cheese, chicken skewers, a beer, and a Moscow mule. 

For this reason I would not go back.

name: Customer_5927
comments:
Good: The food was fantastic. We had a large group (10+) and came here for brunch (and drinks, natch). I had the eggs benedict with short ribs, and loved it. From what I can tell, the rest of the group all enjoyed their dishes as well, from the fried rice breakfast dish to the nachos to the AMAZING peanut butter pancakes. As a starter/side, do not under any circumstances pass up on the "white trash hash" - hasbrowns with white cheddar cheese. YUM.

Bad: The wait was ludicrous. Yes, it was a Saturday, and yes, we had a large group, but Christ Almighty. We waited at the bar (standing room only) for over two hours before being seated. Even if we had split into smaller groups, without a reservation, the wait time would've still been close to an hour and a half. Yikes.

name: Customer_1134
comments: I got the bazooka toast, it was amazing! A little bit pricey but totally worth it. So good it inspired me to give my first yelp review :)

name: Customer_3324
comments:
Tavern is a great brunch place with a good vibe.  I love the sangeria because they top it off with Cava, sortof a sparkling sangeria...refreshing.  I like sitting at the bar because there can be a bit of a wait depending on when you get there.  And in my experience you always get better service at the bar.   
Parking can be hard around midtown so I would valet,  its free, just tip the poor guy!

name: Customer_1078
comments: Burger was amazing.  So juicy, cooked to perfection - ordered it medium rare, and it was!  Fries was delicious as well.  thank you!

name: Customer_6753
comments: Brunch only review. Tavern has delicious brunch that belies its rather generic name. There are some really creative dishes, both sweet and savory. The Shanghai Stirfry is savory breakfast genius: bacon fried rice with an egg on top. So good. My group shared the red velvet pancakes and the cheddar cheese biscuits (with chorizo gravy). Both were pretty good, though I think the red velvet pancakes were a bit sweet. Everyone was happy with their food, and you can't really complain about a 2 for 1 Bloody Mary/Mimosa on a Sunday morning.

name: Customer_4030
comments: Awesome! Great food, great service! Our waitress Rebecca was wonderful! The Moco Loco was amazing!

name: Customer_4809
comments: We walked in without a reservation on Father's Day Sunday at 11 in the morning. We had a flight to catch at 3, so didn't have time to wait and luckily were able to sit at the bar right away. Looking at the menu didn't see anything that looked intriguing or exciting. I was upset that we may have been stuck with some boring brunch on our last day in Nashville. Oh my, was I wrong or what? I ordered the big daddy omelette and my husband got the Huevos Rancheros. I got a big omelet and I couldn't finish it. My omelette was flavorful and the white trash hash was out of this world. I got a fried egg on top of my omelette. What else can you ask for? They also had buy one get one mimosa. Not sure if that was a Father's Day promotion or they do that every Sunday. We also ordered the red velvet waffle for dessert which sounded and looked creative but wasn't that impressive. Overall a great experience and definitely recommend it!!!

name: Customer_2647
comments:
nashville does venice, CA

hipster vibe with delicious morning - buy one get one - drinks.

name: Customer_7571
comments: Our food was pretty. The restaurant is decorated really nice and lots of seating. We got the mussels appetizer which was amazing! I got a wedge salad and my husband got the bbq ribs tacos. I liked talking to the server Zack, he was really nice and a good server. I would go back there just for the mussels!!

name: Customer_7230
comments: Go for the buffalo cauliflower! What better combination could you ask for?! The drinks also are delicious. The space is large and draws a mix after work - a great place for happy hour.

name: Customer_9659
comments: I have never been so insulted and talked down to in my life. Michelle, I think that's her name it's on my receipt but she never introduced herself, was the rudest person I have ever given my money to in my life. When we sat down she was talking about personal issues with the barback loud enough for us to hear and I thought that was odd in and off itself. When she gave us our menus she said a few times "these menus are good for the next 30 seconds."  Sorry but either give us brunch or give us dinner menus and explain that the kitchen is in the midst of a shift change, don't make us feel pressured because you dropped menus that have an extremely short time limit. Instead of eating we decided to just get drinks. She let us know that the brunch menu libations were, her words, 2 for 1. We ordered a mimosa off the list and hung out. When we got get drinks they set two wooden tokens down but didn't reference the at all, so we didn't know what they were for.  Eventually ordered some food off the dinner menu to go. She was very non existent the whole time we were sitting at the bar, not attentive at all. When we asked for the bill I saw that both our drinks were on there. I asked about them and let her know about the 2 for 1 statement she said. She then proceeded to tell me it was buy one, get one and that's what the tokens are for. I told her that "buy one get one" and "2 for 1" are different and if we knew it was BOGO we would have ordered another drink (if she would have even paid attention to us).  After a little back and forth she said she would take care of it and that "they weren't trying to screw us."  She talked to us like we were the worst people on earth because she doesn't know how to explain her own restaurants policies. I work in an industry that has me visiting 10-15 bars/restaurants/hotels a day and I have never had a worse hospitality experience in my life. Tavern Management - this employee is losing you revenue left and right.  Not only is she not taking care of customers and grabbing reorders, she is turning people away for good. This treatment was so horrible and off putting that I am going to go out of my way to recommended against going to Tavern due to the disrespect we felt. Hopefully your floor managers recognize how bad she is and theyo do something about it because she is taking money out of your pocket every shift she works.

name: Customer_5252
comments: Awesome! Great food, great service! Our waitress Rebecca was wonderful! The Moco Loco was amazing!

name: Customer_2284
comments:
So happy we found this cool little spot in the heart of West End during a one-night stay in Nashville. To be concise, here's a rundown of pros/cons:

Pros:
- My boyfriend and I went here around 7 PM on a Tuesday night. It was decently busy, but not overly crowded. We were seated right away. Like.
- The kale salad was life-changing. I waffled for a long time on what to order, and I was NOT disappointed. I couldn't stop eating it! Best salad I've ever had in a restaurant. Get it topped with salmon too. mmm!
- The bf got the fried chicken skins and the beef short rib tacos. He said the tacos were small and not much to them, but overall good flavor and tasty.
- Wine list is great! I got some bubbly and it was reasonably priced.

Cons:
- Service was a bit lacking in my opinion - I get that this is the trendy area, but the vibe seemed a bit pretentious and not very welcoming. [NOTE: If you're from/have spent a considerable amount of time in Chicago, this is a very River North-esque bar. End of story.]
- Beer menu needs some SERIOUS attention. I was shocked there wasn't more quality stuff on that list, hence my choice for wine. Bud and High Life? Come on, man.

Notes:
- A little loud and dark in general - not the best for conversation.
- A lot of TVs all around, so might be fun for gameday, but I can't say for sure.

name: Customer_8434
comments: Cute restaurant and great location. Service was poor. Waitress took 15 minutes to greet us and get our drink orders. Would have been okay, but she had slight attitude the rest of the night and made us seem more like a burden. Food was good. Not great, but good! Also, it was uncomfortably chilly, so bring a jacket.

name: Customer_2763
comments: I visited tavern for lunch looking to try their burger.  I had been told they have one of the best burgers in Nashville.  I thought it was a pretty good burger but I can think of several burgers better in a 5 mile radius.  I will say as a dining venue it is top notch.  Staff was excellent and the layout is very cool.  The menu has several unique items that might bring me back to try like the fried chicken skins...    A tip would be you will probably need to valet since parking is scarce in the area

name: Customer_3300
comments: Nice place. More of a sports bar than I expected, lots of TV's. Good ambience, very good server. Food was good quality, sweet potato fries were great but could of stood to be a little hotter. Food came quick and beer on tap was fresh and of good selection.

name: Customer_3732
comments:
I thought this place was called 'Whiskey Tavern"- That is what the sign said. Its so cool they dropped the Whiskey.  hmm, okay, Tavern it is. Then I kept calling it Whiskey Kitchen because well it is just like Whiskey Kitchen. 

The dark woods, dim light bulbs and limited tables all from IKEAS dark collection, snooty staff, high drink prices and 6 tables on reserved at 5:30 on a Saturday seems a bit weird for a "tavern" 

I went here with a few friends. We just wanted to grab a drink. Even though there were not seats at the bar I proceeded to tell the security-ish hostess we'd just stand and drink our drinks. Seemed like a strange concept to her. We wedged our way in there and was asked if we were waiting for a table. We weren't. The bartender was shocked we were just getting 'drinks'. You won't find a food review here. 

We ordered our drinks and she held her hand out waiting to pay out. No problem. After paying immediately after ordering, we had to drink the drinks.  Lots of huffin and puffin and stink eyes that we were just going to stand there and drink! 

If you like to be 'seen', enjoy bars with chains on the wall, in this room where Tom Edison light bulbs meets LA-tude this is your jam.

name: Customer_1970
comments: Food and service was great! Try the BLT and the egg rolls! The drinks are so good as well.

name: Customer_4848
comments:
Overall: I've only been for brunch and was happy with it soo... nice place to relax and have a little hangover cure on a Saturday or Sunday morning.

Food/Drinks: There are LOTS of brunch options. The Singapore stir fry was great, though it appeared the eggs had been sitting under a heat light for a little while. Still, it was flavorful and not something I've seen anywhere else. I was less impressed with the red velvet waffles. They were extremely dense, and pretty much just tasted like pink waffles. Not bad, just not like red velvet. Be sure to order them with a side of maple syrup, it helps with the density factor. There are a handful of 2fer drink options on the very top of the menu and while they are expensive ($10.50,) from what I've tasted, they're pretty good (and strong.) Go for the blood orange mimosa.

Service/Atmosphere: Our waitress started out being extremely attentive and knowledgeable but kind of dropped off as the meal progressed. That would be understandable if the restaurant had gotten busier but it hadn't. Anyway, she was still nice so I won't complain anymore. The restaurant is very open but seems smaller than when it was under its old name (Lime.) I do like the big open bar, though.

Price: About $40 for 2 people to eat & get a drink a piece for brunch (not including tip)

name: Customer_3838
comments:
I really must admit, I am a fan of some tavern CUISINE.

Lets start with the guacamole.... 
(which is laced with pistachios and goat cheese mind you)
i would say...TO DIE FOR.

The fish taco's are SIMPLY divine, and could quite possibly be my very favorite in all of Nashville.

the Perogies are delish and add a nice touch to the menu... ( i hale from North Eastern Pennsylvania where this particular dish is a standard and i was not disappointed) 

The Shishito Peppers are perfect....
The Salads are fresh and refreshing...

I can not wait to return and sample some more tasty delights.

name: Customer_1238
comments: A friend recommended this restaurant to me while on a business trip to Nashville. The food and service were great! It's a really cool atmosphere with lots of fresh air. Unique menu items, and everything that I saw come out looked so good.

name: Client_6997
comments:
I have seen various reviews on Tavern.  Some very negative.  Others slightly positive.  Most complimented the food but nothing spectacular. 

So, this past Friday night a few friends and I got together for dinner and I wanted to try some place new.  I put out a list of 3 new places (new to me anyway) I'd like to try - based upon the Menu.  I listed Red Pony in Franklin, Burger Up and Tavern.  I sent my friends links to the restaurants and ultimately we agreed that Tavern would be the place.  

We arrived at 7:30 and ended up having to wait an hour for a table and they don't take reservations.  That was fine.  We figured about anywhere we went on a Friday night at this point we would encounter a wait of similar length.  So, we waited and ordered a couple cocktails while we waited.  

This is probably the biggest downside of the restaurant.  They don't have a place for you to really wait.  The bar was jam packed and there was no seating up front.  There was seating outside on the patio - but no one was out there because it was raining and cold.  So, we stood inside near the door for an hour.  

When we were finally seated the server asked us if we needed any more drinks and if we wanted any appetizers.

We decided to go with the 'Bazooka" Guacamole Appetizer.  I pretty much hate Guacamole and never order it anywhere.  I've tried it several times many different places.  Never liked it.  But, this was supposed to be 'different' with some goat cheese and other stuff in it as well.  The presentation of the appetizer was very cool.  They bring it out in a 2-3" deep round cake pan lined with parchment or wax paper - I don't really remember.  Inside there is a glass jar with one of those hinged glass lids on top and its filled with this guacamole concoction.  They have a few chips out on the pan, however, there is also a small, brown paper bag with the logo of 'Tavern' on it - and it is filled with chips.  We took the small server spoon and each took a dollop of the guacamole and put it on a chip.  Wow!  Absolutely incredible.  I don't know if it qualifies as guacamole or not (I'm sure some purists would say it doesn't) - but whatever it is or whatever you want to call it - it was incredible.  I couldn't get enough.  We were scraping the bottom of the jar trying to get every last ounce of this wonderful, tasty spread.

Moving onto dinner two of us go the Tavern Burger.  This burger is made with Prime Rib and Filet.  2 excellent cuts of meat - ground up and made into a burger.  I had mine with White Cheddar and bacon and was incredible!  Everything was good.  The meat, the bacon, the cheese - even the bun was tasty.  My friend had his plain and loved it as well.  Both burgers were served with fries.  He had the regular fries - I had mine tossed in Parmesan and garlic.  Either way they were good.  Apparently they serve them several different ways.

Another friend got the 'Mama Sans Fried Chicken'.  He was blown away by how much food he got.  He also was surprised at how well the chicken went with the cold noodles he was served as the side.  He said the cold noodles were a good juxtaposition against the hot chicken. 

My other friend got the "Salad of Little Gems".  It looked a bit small to me but he claimed to really enjoy it.  As far as salads go it did look great.

The food was all served rather quickly but the pacing of the meal was on point.  The appetizer was served and finished well ahead of the meal making its way from the kitchen.  Too often I feel rushed and sometimes the appetizers and entree arrive within second of each other.  Sometimes even together!  I think the pacing of the meal was excellent.  Also, our server was great and our glasses were never empty.  She made sure we always had plenty to drink.

4 Cocktails, 4 entree's, 1 appetizer = $94 bucks after tax and everything.  So, around 20 bucks a person for a night out.  

So, to review:

Long wait - no place to really sit.  They DO take your phone number and will call you when your table is ready so you can make your way back to the restaurant.

Service was excellent.  Drinks were never empty.  Pacing of meal was great from the appetizer to the main course.

Price was fine.  We could have eaten for less if we didn't get cocktails, appetizers AND the main course.  If we'd just had water and our meal - we would have spent a lot less.  The cocktails were pricy - but pretty stout.  They didn't skimp on the alcohol for sure.

I think it was wonderful and we are already planning our next trip!  I think you should too.

name: Customer_2575
comments: I came here for my birthday brunch and was pleasantly surprised! Our server was wonderful and she talked a lot with us and made the experience even better! Every single dish ordered from our table was delicious! Definitely one of he best brunch places in Nashville!

name: Client_5007
comments:
Had a very pleasant dining experience at Tavern tonight. We arrived at 5 pm and it was pretty dead. It's a big place with a nice outdoor patio and a side patio that can be indoor/outdoor depending on the weather. The vibe seems pretty cool and laid back. Rock music and low lighting get a thumbs up in my book. 

I decided to try a sangria while I browsed over the menu. It did not disappoint. Very fresh and tasty. I decided on The Tavern burger with sweet potato fries. The burger was delicious! It's served on a "meltaway" bun which basically is just a really soft and yummy bun. The sweet potato fries were good as well. Not soggy at all which seems to happen a lot with sweet potato fries. The boyfriend really enjoyed his meal as well but I'll let him tell you about that in his own review. :) Because the dinner was so good, I decided to order a dessert, too. I opted for the cinnamon bread pudding with vanilla gelato on top. It was also delish! It was the perfect amount of sweetness and comfort to end my meal. 

Service was quick and friendly, food was good, and the atmosphere was relaxing. We will definitely be back.

name: Client_5924
comments:
Service was ok, but the food was excellent.  Nothing against our sweet server, but she was alone on a 20 person table - really? I completely blame that one on management! 

Buffalo cauliflower was awesome and the chicken skewers were so so good!  Everyone had a wonderful time! 

Ambiance was so fun!

name: Customer_5323
comments: Just stopped in for drinks.  Staff was great,  never felt rushed. Food passing by smelt and looked awesome. May be coming back tomorrow.

name: Client_4868
comments: Brunch only review. Tavern has delicious brunch that belies its rather generic name. There are some really creative dishes, both sweet and savory. The Shanghai Stirfry is savory breakfast genius: bacon fried rice with an egg on top. So good. My group shared the red velvet pancakes and the cheddar cheese biscuits (with chorizo gravy). Both were pretty good, though I think the red velvet pancakes were a bit sweet. Everyone was happy with their food, and you can't really complain about a 2 for 1 Bloody Mary/Mimosa on a Sunday morning.

name: Customer_8160
comments: Best place within walking distance from my hotel. It's a pretty modern and happening place, with a cool feel to it. I really was looking for a good salad, and was pleasantly surprised with my Junk Salad (romaine, salami, shrimp, olives, pepperoncini, hearts of palm, grape tomato, cucumber, blue cheese, champagne dijon vinaigrette). This was a super tasty salad. I came back 4 days later and had the burger and sweet potato ships. Burger was pretty good, and my only complaint was that the chips were a little on the salty side. Brush some of the salt off and it was good.

name: Customer_7355
comments: Truly not worth the wait. I've tried a couple dishes and nothing has been great- wouldn't really recommend. Almost everything I have tried has either been too dry or too salty. The ambiance is nice but it's pretty slow. The only good food item is their fries.

name: Client_9827
comments: We came here because of all the great yelp reviews, I can't believe this is 4-stars.. Good beer selection, good atmosphere, and decent service.  The food, however, was bla.. We really wanted to try the fried chicken skins, they came out very hard and very stuck together.  The sauce had good flavor but the skins came in a clump that we could hardly break apart. Our food came out about 4 minutes I into our attempt to chisel the skins apart. Kaya toast was weird and really lacked anything to bring the dish together.  After scraping off the sauce it was basically Texas toast and an egg.  The 2 sets of tacos we ordered were both overcooked and VERY dry. Come here for drinks, skip the food!

name: Customer_1769
comments: I usually love this place, but stopped in tonight to place a take out order, and the hostess shewed me off to the absolutely PACKED bar, to try to hail a bartender, on my own, to place an order. This is seriously how you are doing business? We walked out... Ridiculous...

name: Client_7082
comments: Good stuff for brunch if you are drinking. Recommend getting there early as it was packed when we got there around 11 and there was a ton of people waiting when we left.

name: Client_4351
comments:
The simply-named Tavern offers up some mighty simple comfort food pleasures (White Trash hash, anyone?) and elevated junk food game bites. 

That said, I'm not sure this is quite the weekend brunch place for me, due to the TVs providing all of the background noise. I'm not a fan of big TVs blaring games -- to me, this is the worst kind of ambiance. BUT... for those of you seeking a place to watch local sports and cheer on with a crowd, Tavern is the spot for you, especially if your tastes are a bit more high brow than your typical nachos. I mean, they have nachos, but Tavern's come with pistachio and goat cheese. Nice! 

I'd easily return on a non game day (or even to sit on the shaded side patio) for more of that White Trash Hash. Think tater tot casserole. I mean, really. Goodbye hangover. The egg white omelet I had was kinda blah, as the tomatoes made it seem extra watery.The "Wicked" Bloody Mary was hardly wicked, more like gentle, despite the vodka being infused with pickled things that you'd hope for on your glass. They don't automatically garnish the way you'd think. Or at least the way a New Orleanian would think. I mean... just a lime? Nu uh. Our very lovely server came out with some olives for us, which was nice. But a Bloody without beaucoup d' garnish is a naked Mary, indeed.

Extra props for three bottles of hot sauces on the table, marked X, XX and XXX. Go for the orangey habanero, as it's the tastiest of the bunch (it might be the XX). Don't be fooled by the warnings. They are there for the bland American palate.

name: Customer_3245
comments: Got the turkey blt. Excellent! Service was a little slow but we weren't in a rush.

name: Customer_9802
comments:
Not my cuppa gin. Probably because of all that basil.

Tavern is big, a bit brash, bro-friendly with all the TVs and reasonably priced for its prime location on Broadway. Drop your name and cell phone number at the host stand and get sexted when your table is ready. So tech.

Reviews sing praises of their prime beef burgers, so wifey and I opted for a pair, each with bacon and cheese. Subbing a side salad for fries comes with a surcharge... the amount will totally surprise you. (Clickbait header fail: It's $3.50.)

With the fixin's and the greens, a $9.50 patty sizzled up to $16. And the lasting impression is nil, save the need for seasoning and a Maillard crust. It's an average burger that should be $8 at any pub, which gives me pause as to why it comes so highly praised. An off-night in the kitchen? Labor Day weekend lethargy? Unclear. The end result just didn't resonate.

Could cocktails save the day? Her berry julep was all pulp and my 1920 (a gin, grapefruit, ginger and basil concoction borrowed from Brinkley's) tasted only of the green leaf. No tartness, no ginger bite, no other herbal subtleties from the spirit. Just basil. All the basil. At least they were cheap-ish!

name: Client_4946
comments: My favorite place to eat and/or drink in Nashville. It's in midtown, which is local and away from the honky tonks. The ambiance, food, drinks, and service is great. And if anything, there is always good people watching. I come to Tavern after church for brunch, out with my girlfriends for drinks, or out to a nice fun dinner with my boyfriend. My birthday was on a Wednesday last year, which is 2-for-1's night. I came with my girlfriends and had my favorite dessert, their S'mores! So much fun! When asked where do I want to go for brunch? Lunch? Dinner? or just a night out...I always pick Tavern.

name: Client_7468
comments: I don't get it. 4 and 5-start reviews abound, and the weekend brunch line is absurd, but I'd have to describe my experince at Tavern as "just okay." I went here on a Sunday morning ambigudate a month ago. We managed to get bar seating after waiting about 10 minutes, which seemed pretty good compared to the lengthy wait for a real table. The place was bustling, but we didn't have to wait too long to get in our drink orders. That said, while I love deals--and 2-for-1 mimosas and the like qualify--I wasn't bowled over. It tasted like a cheap cava and was heavy on the orange juice. I ordered a burger while my dining companion decided to go with the traditional brunch. My burger was decent but not mouthwateringly amazing, which makes it a far cry from many of the reviews claiming this to be the "best burger in Nashville." Similarly, despite the attempts to make the brunch fare a bit fancier, I wasn't bowled over by any of the flavors. While the prices aren't crazy expensive, they aren't cheap either. Overall I'd describe Tavern as "fine." I'd have no qualms about returning, but the foodie within me doesn't get the hype. Nashville, just because something is dressed up to look fancy and act fancy doesn't mean it's *actually* fancy.

name: Customer_7975
comments: I am now obsessed with Tavern. I'm from out of town and was just in for the weekend, but it was the best meal I have had in awhile (the smoked salmon Benedict w the hash). The hash was unreal! Everyone loved their meals, as well as the great drink specials (buy one get one). The sangria was great on a Saturday morning patio and our server Melissa was so so sweet! Amazing service plus an amazing personality and delicious food. I wish I lived in Nashville so I could eat here weekly. Enjoy it! Cheers!

name: Client_6576
comments: Horrible service! Restaurant was recommended so we decided to check it out. First time in Nashville so we wanted to see what the downtown experince was, and we were greatly disappointed; mostly due to our unfortunate experiance at tavern. We waited for 20 minutes without any acknowledgement from our waiter. When we finally saw him in our area he greeted a table who had just arrived, skipped our table and went on to another. We ended up leaving the establishment. I repeat...horrible service!!!! I guess I can take that back, it wasn't horrible, there WAS NO SERVICE!

name: Customer_6375
comments:
I've never been to an M Street restaurant before, for those of you who are not familiar with M Street they are the zany people who bring us restaurant concepts such as Kayne Prime (on my bucket list,) Virago and Moto (also on my bucket list.) So on Wednesday night we visited Tavern, which is self-described as "a pub for chefs."

Valet parking at this location is a must and they were prompt and efficient. There was plenty of porch seating available as well as being used - Nashvillians do love their porches. The inside of the restaurant had a rustic feel and it seemed as though the bar top was inhabited by business class regulars. That having been said I could easily picture the bar at 12 midnight being inhabited by waitrons and people with checkered pants, it would be a great place to have some concept drinks and small plates after a busy restaurant shift.

I ordered the Korean short rib tacos - I definitely got the red pepper forward taste as well as the cool of the cucumber and cilantro. I would order it again. Delivery time was about 13 minutes, a good ticket time.

It's very evident that these people are "on their game," I will be returning to try other items on their menu. And one day I will visit Kayne Prime, I might splurge for that on my father's birthday. Visit Tavern, have fun!

name: Client_2821
comments: I'm usually a chilaquiles girl, so the Huevos Rancheros sounded sort of tempting with its eggs, tortillas and salsa combination. Now, huevos rancheros in general has never really appealed to me, but Tavern had me changing my tune. I have a feeling that no other restaurant's version of this dish will impress me as much as this one, but if you are in Nashville and you are at Tavern for brunch and you don't get the Huevos Rancheros.... you're making a HUGE mistake. One of the best brunch meals of my life y'all...

name: Client_4766
comments: Came for brunch on Fathers Day, packed!  We were able to get a spot at the bar right away and ate there. Food was above average and the bartenders were quick and attentive.

name: Customer_3780
comments: PSA: Just go for the 2 for 1 drink special at brunch and white trash hash. The atmosphere is trendy. Everything else is not worth the wait! We arrived at 11am on a Friday for brunch, was told the wait was 20 mins. We did not get seated until 11:50a. Food is average. I will say the nachos were good but nothing outstanding. The biscuits came out cold. A "side" of bacon is $5 dollars and you get seriously 2 slices. Service was very very slow. Wouldn't recommend unless you have 3.5 hours or more to kill for brunch.

name: Customer_8154
comments:
My friend and I were visiting Nashville and found this place through a quick google search. We were staying downtown, so it was a quick and cheap cab ride away (5 minutes/$7 ride). We went on a Saturday night, so there was about an hour wait. We decided to grab a drink at the bar (no wait there) and stood around chatting/playing a charades game on our phone...which helped pass the time! The drinks were avg. $10/piece. Not cheap, but normal for this kind of restaurant. 

Once we were seated, we knew we wanted to try their french fries (we had previously scoped out the menu) and quickly ordered the sweet potato ones. She ordered the mahi sandwich and I went with the chicken tikka masala, Both were very good.

Would recommend and return!

name: Client_1852
comments: Great food!  The menu is full of interesting, and unique items.  I tried the smoked salmon eggs benedict, and it was phenomenal.  The interior is very well decorated, and the servers were helpful and prompt.  Though it was a little on the expensive side, it was well worth the cost for such a great experience.

name: Client_9885
comments: Amazing food, great service! Melissa was so accommodating! We got seated right away too.

name: Client_9735
comments: This place was very modern and chic! Very cool look and feel of the resturant. We only came in for a quick bite to eat and some drinks to start off the night. For a Saturday night around 7pm, it was pretty busy. Definitely a loud place because of all the people, but they played good music. Ambiance is casual but not too dressed down. I wouldn't wear a hoodie and sweats, but dressy casual. Service was good. We had the buffalo cauliflower and it was delicious! Will def be back when I'm in Nashville again!

name: Customer_4649
comments:
We wanted to check this place out after seeing the great reviews. 
Arrived on Thursday (New Years Day) around noon and the place was packed with a hour and a half wait. We put our name in and went next door for a drink, 
The restaurant texted us when our table was ready and also had a cool app that you can check your place in line. 
Only had drinks and a few apps. The tuscan fries were good but had a LOT of garlic.
My friend loved her Kale salad. 
If you like a bloody mary, try the cucumber mary made with cucumber vodka. It was unbelievable. 

This was hands down out favorite place in Nashville and this place had the BEST service we got our whole trip. A+ to the staff. We were really really impressed. 
We went back on Friday night around 1am and it was pretty empty. The guy sitting next to us said its really a better brunch or Sunday Funday bar and not busy at night.

name: Client_6915
comments: We walked in without a reservation on Father's Day Sunday at 11 in the morning. We had a flight to catch at 3, so didn't have time to wait and luckily were able to sit at the bar right away. Looking at the menu didn't see anything that looked intriguing or exciting. I was upset that we may have been stuck with some boring brunch on our last day in Nashville. Oh my, was I wrong or what? I ordered the big daddy omelette and my husband got the Huevos Rancheros. I got a big omelet and I couldn't finish it. My omelette was flavorful and the white trash hash was out of this world. I got a fried egg on top of my omelette. What else can you ask for? They also had buy one get one mimosa. Not sure if that was a Father's Day promotion or they do that every Sunday. We also ordered the red velvet waffle for dessert which sounded and looked creative but wasn't that impressive. Overall a great experience and definitely recomand it!!!

name: Customer_1019
comments: Y'all gave my Asian friend and my white friend some food poisoning from the Caesar salad. Thanks Obama.

name: Customer_2040
comments: Great spot to come to if your in Nashville. The have one the best drink deals you can find on thursdays and Saturday's and Sunday's. Food is okay.

name: Customer_4037
comments:
Unfortunately they don't take reservations.  It was a crazy busy weekend and took about an hour to be seated.
Sat on porch behind bar, they had propane heaters so it was plenty warm despite 15 degree weather.
Service was very attentive and friendly.  Food was great. Shasito peppers were perfect. Cauliflower was good and smoking hot spicy.
Glad we waited.

name: Customer_8878
comments: So cute! A must stop on your Nashville adventure!!! Cutest drinks and brunch spot. I got the red sangria and an egg white and fruit brunch. My friends for mimosas. We are all so happy!

name: Customer_2664
comments:
Stopped in at lunch for THE Tavern Burger.  While it is the only burger on the menu, they provide many options for it.  While I didn't personally order it, a coworker got a cooked egg on it,  You can get it also with Grilled Onions or Bacon.

The burger is pretty sizable and also includes Belgian fries. I'm not sure exactly what they do to Begian-ize them, butt he were quite good.

We arrived at just a bit after 11 AM so it wasn't very busy yet. Parking could certainly be an issue though.

15 dollars for a burger might also be a bit pricier that a regular Joe or Jane is willing to pay, and it would be hard to argue.  It was however, quite delicious and filling.

I'm not sure what the dinner time crowd looks like, but at least for THE Burger I would be back.

name: Client_7108
comments: We were scouting for a place to rent out for a company retreat dinner. Unfortunately, they don't allow dogs on the patio, and I has my 2 small dogs. I'd understand this if you couldn't access the patio, but theirs is easily accessible from the front door and the street. I don't know what moron made the no dogs on the open air patio rule, but they should reconsider. That said, I did not eat here, went up the street to eat. The two stars were earned by the hostess, who was lovely and apologetic. I wish her the best and hope she finds employment at a better run establishment. We will be spending our decently sized budget elsewhere. Gracias por nada Tavern.

name: Client_1192
comments: Went today with a group for brunch. We had no complaints. Great-cucumber Bloody Mary, coffee, lobster gumbo, grilled artichoke, white trash hash and service. The decor was tasteful and semi modern. I definitely felt like we left Nashville for a couple hours which was great! Will definitely be back!

name: Customer_8765
comments:
What I liked:
1. White Trash Hash- With a name like that, what's there not to like?  While I'm sure I could re-create this for about $2 (smashed fried hashbrowns smothered in cheese), it was well worth the extra cost to enjoy at brunch.  YUM!
2. Brunch Menu- There were too many delicious options to choose.  I went with a salad, but everything (especially the burger and french toast) looked and smelled fantastic.
3. Bloody Marys- They served my favorite, Zig-Zag mix and you get 2 for the price they charge.

What I didn't like:
1. This place gets VERY crowded on the weekend during the brunch rush.  We were quoted at hour+ wait shortly after they opened and ended up just snagging a seat at the bar.
2. Service- The bartender was understaffed and a bit slow to respond to requests.  They also forgot about part of our order and had to be reminded.

Overall Verdict: Make a reservation or show-up early and prepare to wait.  Get the white trash hash and enjoy delicious brunch!

name: Customer_1306
comments: We went for lunch today. Service was too slow for anyone on a lunch break (it took nearly an hour). There wasn't a lunch menu, so we paid dinner prices for dinner portions. I saw a little section of "fast plates". I forget what it was called, but none of those items really jumped out at me. We ordered fish tacos, beef tacos with Korean BBQ and fries. It was all good. This might be a better place for dinner.

name: Client_7038
comments: Best brunch! Came here on a busy Saturday with a group of girls. Everyone loved their food and drinks! Waitress was friendly, efficient and knowledgeable about all menu and drink items. Would definetly come here again.

name: Client_7108
comments: Food was great here! I've been here before just for drinks and wanted to come back because I had an amazing pineapple charred mule cocktail. We came back and ate this time. The only thing preventing me from giving Tavern five stars was that the service was slower than it should be and it wasn't an insanely busy night. Our waitress was not the most attentive.

name: Customer_2548
comments: Great atmosphere. Amazing burgers. The heart of Nashville in food. Would definitely come again and recommend to friends visiting Nashville.

name: Client_6556
comments:
Not my kind of place but I think if it was it would be fantastic! 
Loud music, sports on big TV s, huge bar, inside or outside seating. Friendly attentive staff, food artsy. Served lightning fast. Very clean and beautifully decorated. Enjoyed my Burger very much. Micheal loved his Junk Salad... Great place for those who like what I described.

name: Client_3274
comments: My favorite place to eat and/or drink in Nashville. It's in midtown, which is local and away from the honky tonks. The ambiance, food, drinks, and servise is great. And if anything, there is always good people watching. I come to Tavern after church for brunch, out with my girlfriends for drinks, or out to a nice fun dinner with my boyfriend. My birthday was on a Wednesday last year, which is 2-for-1's night. I came with my girlfriends and had my favorite dessert, their S'mores! So much fun! When asked where do I want to go for brunch? Lunch? Dinner? or just a night out...I always pick Tavern.

name: Customer_7869
comments: Don't order the fish tacos- they were very disappointing. I didn't even want to eat them. Order the burger. It was very good. Restaurant is a little overpriced for what it is.

name: Customer_7861
comments: Oh, Brunch at Tavern. I'm so sad that it took me so long to visit you. I'll keep this brief: The dishes here are superbly crafted. Flavors are lovely and multifaceted, and the plating is gorgeous. My favorite dishes, though, are easy to pinpoint. First up is the Sweet Potato Chips, which arrive at your table with a curry salt and blue cheese fondue. This is a perfect start to any meal, and honestly, I could probably be happy just munching on these while sipping a few cocktails (which I'll get to in a moment). As for a main course, though: The Benedict Dos. Poached eggs, smoked salmon, and a creamy hollandaise? Delicious doesn't even begin to cover it. I will admit that I find myself rather addicted to their Blood Orange Mimosa, so I haven't actually tried anything else on the menu. However, one of my closest friends loved the Bloody Mary, and their beer selection is impressive and was mat with easy approval from our group a few weeks ago. Is it loud? Yes. Is it expensive? Sure, although most of the cocktails are two for one. But is it worth the insanely long wait? Absolutely.

name: Client_8643
comments: I went to Tavern on a Saturday night and waited about 20 minutes for our table for 2, which really is pretty good! We ordered a few plates to share- egg rolls, fish tacos and Tuscan fries. The egg rolls were served with queso and salsa... for a Chinese food... that was weird. When I've had garlic Parmesan fries in the past, they're usually served with a dipping sauce of some kind,  but these were not. We were given a heaping serving of them that 2 of us couldn't finish though. The fish tacos were by far the best dish we had- HIGHLY recommend them! Our waitress was very nice, though it took her quite a few minutes to actually come over to us initially to take drink orders. Other than that she was wonderful. We each ordered a cocktail and they were strong for sure- I was just unimpressed with both. The julep was decent. The second drink was a grapefruit/lemon lime/ vodka drink that tasted like I drank straight grapefruit juice instead of a mixed drink... to be fair, the waitress did ask if I wanted it remade. The ambiance was great, and it was definitely crowded. They had a DJ playing music and it was a younger crowd.

name: Customer_5558
comments: Jalepeno margaritas. Grilled artichokes. Mac and cheese. Amazing.

name: Customer_5436
comments: Terrible wait (unnecessary), average service, above average prices, and excruciating wait for food. Find someplace else. There's lots to choose from.

name: Customer_2752
comments: I really must admit, I am a fan of some tavern CUISINE. Lets start with the guacamole.... (which is laced with pistachios and goat cheese mind you) i would say...TO DIE FOR. The fish taco's are SIMPLY divine, and could quite possibly be my very favorite in all of Nashville. the Perogies are delish and add a nice touch to the menu... ( i hale from North Eastern Pennsylvania where this particular dish is a standard and i was not disappointed) The Shishito Peppers are perfect.... The Salads are fresh and refreshing... I can not wait to return and sample some more tasty delights.

name: Client_8315
comments:
This place is awesome!  We stumbled upon it after checking into our hotel...we wanted to walk around after being in the car for 9 hours and we were starving.  We got a table outside, it was loud, but what do you expect on a Friday night in early summer?
The food was great....I got the Nuevo Israeli bread salad and my husband got the turkey blt (with sweet potato chips (YUMMMM)--both fantastic.  
They have an extensive drink/beer list and the staff is knowledgeable about the beer they serve and didn't steer my husband wrong.  
Would recommend trying this place out if you haven't already.

name: Client_5616
comments: Excellent service, has air conditioning which is great in the south, my favorite was the chicken chicharrón "chicharrón" good location in the block is the best one!

name: Customer_8313
comments: Seriously, the best place I've been to in Nashville (so far). The food was excellent, and there is plenty of variety to make everyone happy. Definitely eating here again soon.

name: Customer_3747
comments: You'll definetly have a wait for brunch but grab a drink and buckle in cause it's worth it. Everyone at the table loved what they ordered. We started with the buffalo cauliflower and got the pretzel pancakes, nooner, blueberry waffle and the red velvet waffle and damn if we didn't clean our plates. Also if you don't get the white trash hash you'll regret it for years to come. Service was great and our drinks were perfect.
